💡 Key Takeaways
  • Prior to the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 today, Rockstar had been doing its utmost to play just about every aspect of the game’s production outside of explicitly-revealed details as close to the vest as possible.
  • One of those details, and arguably one of the most crucial to the production, is the game’s cast of voice actors.
  • Now that the game is out, the full cast list has been revealed via the in-game credits, which you technically don’t even need to finish the game to see.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prior to the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 today, Rockstar had been doing its utmost to play just about every aspect of the game’s production outside of explicitly-revealed details as close to the vest as possible. That’s the whole reason why that little saga of GTA 6 leaks was such a big deal, because so much about the game was in a proverbial black box before launch. Now, though, the game is finally in the world’s collective hands, and that means every little itty-bitty detail is readily-available for everyone to obsessively comb through.

One of those details, and arguably one of the most crucial to the production, is the game’s cast of voice actors. Ahead of the game’s release, the vast majority of the cast was shrouded in mystery, with the single exception being veteran actor Stephen Root revealing his role as Brian Heder, though naturally, that didn’t stop the rampant speculation from the precious few soundbites we got in the trailers.

Now that the game is out, the full cast list has been revealed via the in-game credits, which you technically don’t even need to finish the game to see. Perhaps unsurprisingly for such a high-profile production, many of the game’s voice actors come from TV and film backgrounds, a testament to Rockstar’s star power magnetism.

First and foremost, let’s get into our two lead characters, and the most important roles in GTA 6, Jason and Lucia, the duo that had successfully captured hearts and minds before the game was even out. Jason is voiced by Dylan Rourke, a television actor who has had a small spattering of roles since 2013, with some standouts including Modern Family, Grey’s Anatomy, Station 19, and In the Vault.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Lucia, the series's first female protagonist, is voiced by Manni L. Perez, who has previously provided incidental roles in GTA 5 and GTA Online. Outside of games, she’s had a lot of experience in various crime demonstrates, such as The Blacklist, Chicago P.D., and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.

Jason is voiced by Dylan Rourke [...] Lucia, meanwhile, is voiced by Manni L. Perez.

Surprisingly, one of the biggest names in the cast aside from the aforementioned Stephen Root is Bobby Moynihan in the role of Jason’s bumbling buddy Cal. Moynihan is a seasoned actor who got his start all the way back in 1996 with roles in live-action and animated film and television like Portlandia, Aqua Teen Hunger Force, and We Bare Bears, though his most decorated gig was various roles on Saturday Night Live since 2008, most notably his recurring character on the “Weekend Patch” sketches.

It has been revealed that some other names dropped in the credits include Dre'Quan as Naiqui Macabroad, Orlagh Cassidy as Lori Heder, Brad Carter as Donnie, Mallory Wu as Andy, and rappers Hood Brat and Krissy Celess as Bae-Luxe and Roxy Rashad, respectively. You can check out the credits yourself either by beating the game or just checking the in-game settings menu.

According to recent reports, if I were a betting man, I’d put money down on most, if not all of the biggest names in this cast making appearances at The Game Awards next month. In fact, Manni L. Perez has already been nominated for Best Performance as Lucia, among the many, many other categories that GTA 6 has been nominated for alongside Game of the Year.

It’s gonna be a star-studded event, as it often is, of course, but by appearing in the biggest game of the release, quite possibly the entire decade, just about everyone in the GTA 6 cast have just earned some major street cred in the entertainment industry. Obviously, Stephen Root and Bobby Moynihan were already well-established actors, but hopefully, we’ll be seeing a lot more of Dylan Rourke and Manni L. Perez both in and out of the gaming scene going forward.

Industry observers note that you leave a mark like that on entertainment history, and people will start actively seeking you out in every other production you appear in. Hey, maybe they’ll make cameos if we ever get a GTA movie.

Industry observers note that T1 has added two-time Masters champion Tyson 'TenZ' Ngo to its Valorant roster for VCT Pacific in 2027. The move ends his retirement and builds on T1's signing of crashies, who has just left London-based Fnatic.

T1 has ended Tyson ‘TenZ’ Ngo’s retirement. The organisation confirmed on 12 November that he will join its Valorant roster for VCT Pacific in 2027. It made the announcement with a post and a welcome video.

T1 called him a ‘living legend’ of Valorant. It said he was starting a new chapter with the organisation.

In a recent development, tenZ retired from professional play in 2024. He has spent this year at T1 as a content creator. The announcement moves him from that role into the competitive squad.

It has been revealed that his record explains the attention. With Sentinels, he beat Fnatic 3-0 in the Masters Reykjavík 2021 final. He then won Masters Madrid 2024 with a 3-2 win over Gen.G. That made him the first Americas player to win more than one VCT Masters event, Liquipedia records.

It has been revealed that the TenZ news came a day after T1 confirmed Austin ‘crashies’ Roberts. He returns six years after T1 released him in September 2020. crashies called T1 the place ‘where it all started’. He noted he was excited for the upcoming challenge.

He played for Fnatic from 11 December 2024 until 4 November 2026. He joined T1 on 11 November 2026.

According to recent reports, his exit is part of a wider reshuffle at the London-based organisation. Fnatic lost the Masters Toronto 2025 grand final 3-1 to Paper Rex. It then lost the Valorant Champions 2025 grand final in Paris 3-2 to NRG. On 2 November, Fnatic released head coach Andrey ‘ENGH’ Sholokhov. It said it was making changes ahead of the 2027 season.

According to recent reports, T1 has also kept some continuity. It extended BuZz’s contract on 6 November 2026. The newly introduced deal runs until the end of 2028.

The VCT structure for 2027 was confirmed on 28 October. Under it, the eight Pacific partner teams go straight into Kickoff in January 2027. The other four Kickoff places go to teams from regional open qualifiers.

The KING is back! 👑A living legend of VALORANT, 'TenZ' begins a fresh chapter with T1.Ready to make history under the red wings, join us in giving him a warm welcome!

📺 https://t.co/ny3VtTtYnx#T1VALORANT pic.twitter.com/gmgLEzXJR2.

— T1 VALORANT (@T1) November 12, 2026.

Sources indicate that before Kickoff, T1 has a date in Los Angeles. It is one of six teams directly invited to Red Bull Home Ground 2026. Fnatic, Sentinels, G2 Esports, NRG and ZETA DIVISION have also been invited. That puts the former clubs of both TenZ and crashies in the same field as T1.

Recent findings suggest that the event runs from 10 to 13 December. Group stage matches are on 10 and 11 December. Bracket play and the semi-finals follow on 12 December. The grand final is on 13 December.

  • Industry observers note that jacob Novak, former financial lead at Square Enix, is one such person.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is finally here, and it's already smashing records, standing as the highest-rated game of all time with just one day under its belt – but that might not be enough to save developer Rockstar Games from further rounds of layoffs, some believe.

Industry observers note that jacob Novak, former financial lead at Square Enix, is one such person. Taking to X to share his thoughts on potential Rockstar redundancies – a topic that's been circulating following words from animation programmer Nestor Uriarte – he asserts, "There will, of course, be major layoffs at Rockstar." After all, "They've built the biggest, most expensive game of all time and now released it." But why does that matter?

Industry observers note that well, it boils down to the "team size" Rockstar required during production versus what it needs now, post-launch, according to Novak. "Part of the team will move onto GTA 6's online mode, part to DLC, but the team size required to ship this is not the team size required to build continuous content." It's a tough thought to consider, but I suppose it does make a bit of sense – although that's not to say it guarantees layoffs.

Industry observers note that novak believes they're incoming, however. "It's likely that Rockstar has been waiting until after the game ships, not wanting the layoffs to impact the news cycle or distract in reviews." he writes. "My guess is early Q1 next year with a consulting period starting in the UK." He means early 2027 here, which is only a few months off at this point. The executive cites Take-Two Interactive's finances in a reply then.

https://t.co/J6EUe8qrjaNovember 19, 2026.

It has been revealed that attached is a screenshot of a Google search reading, "What was the last profitable quarter for Take-Two [Interactive]?" Its results state that Take-Two's last profitable quarter was back in 2022. Alongside the image, Novak indicates "Strauss Zelnick's mission is not going to be to let the profits be absorbed by keeping employees. It is going to be to recoup all his losses." It isn't set in stone, obviously, but it certainly provokes some thought.

It sadly wouldn't be a first for Rockstar, with its "ruthless" 2025 layoffs springing to mind immediately – but it's something I do hope we don't see come to fruition, especially when considering the success that GTA 6 is seeing so far.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that dota 2 will return to the Riyadh-hosted Esports World Cup in 2027, though dates, format and prize money are still to come. The title has never been won twice, and its prize pool has fallen at every edition so far.

Industry observers note that dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was announced without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams. The whole event is listed for July to August 2027.

The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.

It has been revealed that the first edition, Riyadh Masters 2024, carried a US$5,000,000 prize pool. In 2025 Team Spirit took US$1,000,000 from a US$3,000,000 pool in a 16-team event. The 2026 tournament ran from 7 to 19 July with 24 teams. That field was eight teams larger than a year earlier.

The winner still takes a large share. PARIVISION collected US$750,000, or 37.5% of the pool, plus 1,000 Club Championship points. Runners-up BetBoom Team received US$340,000 and 750 points, Liquipedia reported.

In a recent development, those points feed into a larger prize. In 2026 the Club Championship paid US$30 million across the top 24 clubs. The champion club received US$7 million from an overall event prize pool of US$75 million. AG.AL won it with 5,300 points, stopping Team Falcons from winning a third title in a row. For organisations weighing the cost of a Dota 2 roster, that club prize is part of the calculation.

In a recent development, not every club is staying. Falcons released all five players from the roster that won The International 2025, according to Timesaver.gg.

Industry observers note that no club or player has won the event’s Dota 2 title more than once. Each of the three editions went to a different club with a different roster. Gaimin Gladiators beat Team Liquid in the 2024 final. A year later, Team Spirit swept Team Falcons 3-0. As the 2026 champions, PARIVISION now get the first chance to defend the title.

It has been revealed that PVISION are your Dota 2 at EWC26 Champions! 👏 pic.twitter.com/34U67Oaj7G.

— Esports World Cup (@EWC_EN) July 20, 2026.

Their rivals arrive in form. Team Spirit went out of the 2026 event before the final. A month later, they won The International 2026 in Shanghai. Yatoro and Collapse became the first players to win three Internationals. Team Yandex finished third at both the 2026 Esports World Cup and The International. After signing ATF, they won PGL Wallachia Season 9 and BLAST SLAM VIII.

The route into the event is taking shape. The organiser’s Road to EWC qualifier programme for 2027 aims to involve 1.8 million players across more than 400 events. Qualifier slots for each game will be confirmed later. Counter-Strike 2, already confirmed for both 2027 and 2028, will hold a 32-team event in Riyadh from 20 July to 1 August 2027.

There had also been no reports of cases where the leaked information had been misused as of the time Sega made their announcement. The tech giant have naturally put distributing any further email newsletters through Arara on hold until their investigation's done and proposal to reach out to each affected person individually once the full details of the leak have been confirmed.

Rockstar Is Promoting GTA 6 in a Country Where It Can't Officially Sell It

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that rockstar is promoting Grand Theft Auto 6 to players in mainland China, even though the game hasn't been approved for official sale there.
  • Recent findings suggest that according to a Reuters report published on November 18, Rockstar posted a GTA 6 preorder-related video on Douyin, the Chinese counterpart to TikTok, on November 12.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Douyin account is verified under Rockstar International Limited and demonstrated a Shanghai IP location when Reuters reviewed it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that rockstar is promoting Grand Theft Auto 6 to players in mainland China, even though the game hasn't been approved for official sale there. It's an unusual situation for one of the biggest launches of the year, but the organization's social media activity makes it clear that Chinese players are still part of the audience it's trying to reach.

Recent findings suggest that according to a Reuters report published on November 18, Rockstar posted a GTA 6 preorder-related video on Douyin, the Chinese counterpart to TikTok, on November 12. The video encouraged users to preload the game ahead of its worldwide November 19 release.

Recent findings suggest that the Douyin account is verified under Rockstar International Limited and demonstrated a Shanghai IP location when Reuters reviewed it. By November 18, it had attracted around 480,000 followers and more than 300,000 likes. That's a sizeable audience for a game that can't be sold through officially approved channels in mainland China.

In a recent development, the promotion itself isn't complicated. Rockstar was telling fans that GTA 6 was available to preload on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, just as it had been doing for players elsewhere. What's unusual is the market receiving that message.

It has been revealed that reuters was able to access both the account and its promotional video in China. Neither Rockstar nor the National Press and Publication Administration, the country's regulator, had responded to the publication's requests for comment when the report was filed.

This isn't the same as Rockstar announcing an official Chinese release. A social media promotion doesn't mean GTA 6 has been approved for official sale in mainland China. The studio also hasn't mentioned that an approved release is on the way.

According to recent reports, imported video games have to pass a government approval process before they can be officially sold in mainland China. The authorities scrutinize content such as violence, sexual material, and politically sensitive themes. Given what Grand Theft Auto is about, it's not difficult to see why the series might face obstacles.

Reuters reports that the Grand Theft Auto franchise has never received official approval for sale in mainland China. GTA 6 is also missing from the regulator's published lists of approved imported games. That's the key point here. It's not a fresh announcement that the game has been banned outright, but rather that it lacks the approval required for an official domestic release.

A social media promotion doesn't mean GTA 6 has been approved for official sale in mainland China.

Recent findings suggest that the contrast is particularly striking because Rockstar is treating GTA 6 as a worldwide event. The game rolled out on November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and its marketing has reached far beyond the countries where ordinary retail sales are available.

Recent findings suggest that of course, an official sales restriction doesn't necessarily stop people from playing the game. Reuters states Chinese players have been using foreign console accounts or buying imported boxed editions that include download codes. One Douyin user who said he was in Beijing posted about obtaining a Hong Kong edition for roughly 500 yuan, or about $75.

That doesn't make those purchases part of an officially approved Chinese distribution channel. It simply shows that a market can exist for a game even when the usual local release process isn't available.

It's also worth distinguishing China's situation from the ratings concerns seen in other territories. GTA 6 almost ran into trouble in South Korea, but the matter in mainland China concerns the separate approval system for imported games. They aren't interchangeable cases.

Sources indicate that for now, Rockstar can speak to a substantial Chinese audience while GTA 6 remains unavailable for officially approved domestic sales. Whether that situation changes is something only a later regulatory decision could settle. Until then, its Douyin account is a reminder that the game's reach doesn't end at the borders of its official markets.

Industry News: This remarkable upcoming material could solve a major carbon capture problem

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1149 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A newly developed material from Oregon State University could help solve one of the biggest challenges in industrial carbon capture: removing carbon dioxide from emissions that contain large amounts of water vapor.
  • Recent findings suggest that the researchers have filed a patent application for the innovation, which belongs to a class of materials known as metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs.
  • The advance could have important implications for reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A newly developed material from Oregon State University could help solve one of the biggest challenges in industrial carbon capture: removing carbon dioxide from emissions that contain large amounts of water vapor. Instead of allowing moisture to interfere with the process, the material uses it to help maintain effective carbon capture.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers have filed a patent application for the innovation, which belongs to a class of materials known as metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs. Their findings, published in Angewandte Chemie, could help make carbon capture more practical and affordable for factories and other industrial facilities.

The advance could have important implications for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Industrial operations, including the burning of fossil fuels to produce energy, are major sources of atmospheric carbon dioxide. In the United States, industry accounts for 30% of total greenhouse gas emissions, according to the Environmental Protection Agency.

A Upcoming Material That Overcomes a Major Carbon Capture Problem.

According to recent reports, the new material, called BVR-X, has an unusual internal structure that keeps water and carbon dioxide largely separated within its microscopic pores. By directing the two substances into different regions, it prevents water molecules from occupying the spaces needed to capture carbon dioxide.

"This internal organization helps the material work under conditions that more closely resemble real industrial emissions," stated Kyriakos Stylianou, professor of chemistry in the OSU College of Science.

In a recent development, MOFs are crystalline materials built from positively charged metal ions connected by organic molecules called ligands, which act as linkers. The metal ions form connection points, or nodes, while the linkers join them together into repeating structures resembling tiny cages. These structures contain extremely small pores that can trap gas molecules on their internal surfaces through a process called adsorption, much like a sponge holds substances within its structure.

One of the advantages of MOFs is their remarkable adaptability. Scientists can combine different metals and organic linkers to create materials with specific characteristics. According to Stylianou, millions of MOF designs are theoretically possible. Researchers have already synthesized more than 100,000 distinct MOFs and predicted the properties of hundreds of thousands more.

Why Carbon Capture Needs Better Materials.

Recent findings suggest that "The capture of CO2 is critical for meeting net-zero emission targets," remarked Stylianou, who directs OSU's Materials Discovery Laboratory, known as the MaD Lab. "MOFs have shown a lot of promise because of their porosity and their structural versatility.".

Sources indicate that carbon dioxide is a major greenhouse gas released when fossil fuels are burned. As it accumulates in the atmosphere, it traps heat and contributes to global warming.

Industry observers note that one approach to addressing the problem involves removing carbon dioxide directly from the atmosphere. Facilities designed for this purpose are beginning to operate in different parts of the world. The world's largest such plant opened in Iceland in 2024, although its annual carbon removal capacity is still relatively small compared with global emissions. According to Stylianou, the facility can capture roughly as much carbon dioxide in one year as about 7,200 cars produce over the same period.

Industry observers note that capturing carbon dioxide before it reaches the atmosphere is another option, and the technologies used for this purpose are considerably more established. At factories and power plants, carbon capture systems can intercept emissions as they travel through exhaust systems and smokestacks. Some of these systems use MOFs to adsorb carbon dioxide molecules from the passing gases.

How Water Makes Industrial Carbon Capture Difficult.

A major obstacle, however, is that industrial exhaust often contains substantial amounts of water vapor. Many MOFs that perform well in controlled laboratory experiments lose much of their carbon capture ability when exposed to the humid conditions found in actual smokestacks.

The gases can be dried before carbon dioxide is removed, but doing so requires additional equipment and energy. Those costs can become so significant that the overall process is no longer economically practical for industrial use.

Sources indicate that BVR-X offers a different approach. Rather than requiring moisture to be removed, the material responds to water in a way that preserves its ability to collect carbon dioxide. Its internal organization allows water and carbon dioxide to occupy different regions, helping prevent the competition that normally undermines carbon capture performance.

It has been revealed that "Water usually makes capturing carbon dioxide more difficult," he stated. "Our new material does something unusual: It responds to water by changing in a way that lets it keep capturing CO2 effectively even under very humid conditions.".

Strong Performance Under Realistic Industrial Conditions.

Laboratory tests demonstrated that BVR-X could efficiently capture carbon dioxide from a highly humid gas stream containing only 4% carbon dioxide.

Sources indicate that that concentration is particularly relevant to emissions from burning natural gas, where carbon dioxide makes up a relatively small proportion of the exhaust. Extracting it becomes especially difficult when large quantities of water vapor are also present.

The experiments therefore tested the material under conditions that resemble an important real-world challenge, "where separating a small amount of CO2 in the presence of substantial water is particularly challenging," noted Stylianou.

It has been revealed that the researchers also found that BVR-X could repeatedly capture and release carbon dioxide without losing its effectiveness over dozens of cycles. This ability to regenerate the material is important because commercial carbon capture systems must reuse their capture materials many times to keep operating costs manageable.

Sources indicate that "And the material can be regenerated and reused, maintaining performance through dozens of capture-and-release cycles and tolerating demanding conditions," he added. "Those are notable qualities for practical carbon-capture technologies.".

The results suggest that BVR-X could help overcome a major limitation of existing MOF technologies, particularly in industrial settings where removing moisture from exhaust gases would otherwise be costly.

The study brought together researchers from several institutions. Stylianou worked with MaD Lab members Ankit Yadav, Emmanuel Musa and Andrzej Gładysiak, along with Micah Hickethier, Chun-Wai Chang and Kai Shen Choong from the Oregon State College of Engineering.

Additional collaborators included scientists from the University of California, Berkeley; the University of Oregon; and the ARAMCO Research and Development Center.

Funding was provided by Saudi Aramco, the Murdock Charitable Trust, and a donor-advised fund established by Oregon State University alumni and retired public school teachers Brian and Marilyn Kleiner through the OSU Foundation.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch.
  • Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a latest blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing concerns with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.
  • We know that Season 2 is introducing a big fresh map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the newly introduced content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a latest blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing concerns with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a big fresh map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the upcoming season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

Sources indicate that BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Recent findings suggest that movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Industry observers note that audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

#5368. Why obesity affects men and women differently may be hiding in their fat

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1118 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Why obesity affects men and women differently may be hiding in their fat

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1118 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, scientists at the University of California, Riverside have uncovered a surprising difference in how the immune systems of males and females respond to obesity.
  • The discovery centers on eosinophils, immune cells best known for their involvement in allergies and asthma.
  • According to recent reports, the study, published in PNAS Nexus, was led by University of California, Riverside biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, scientists at the University of California, Riverside have uncovered a surprising difference in how the immune systems of males and females respond to obesity. Their findings suggest that certain immune cells found in body fat can help protect against inflammation and metabolic problems, while others may make these harmful effects worse.

The discovery centers on eosinophils, immune cells best known for their involvement in allergies and asthma. In experiments with mice, researchers found that these cells behave differently depending on biological sex, potentially helping explain why obesity does not affect males and females in the same way.

According to recent reports, the study, published in PNAS Nexus, was led by University of California, Riverside biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik. Their findings challenge the longstanding assumption that eosinophils are largely similar cells with relatively few specialized functions. The results also point toward potential new approaches for treating obesity and its complications.

Six Types of Immune Cells Found in Body Fat.

According to recent reports, to investigate the role of eosinophils in obesity, the researchers used high-resolution single-cell sequencing, a technique that allows scientists to examine gene activity in individual cells. They identified six distinct eosinophil populations in adipose (fat) tissue, each with its own pattern of gene expression and potentially different biological functions.

This unexpected diversity suggests that eosinophils play a much more complicated role in metabolic health than previously recognized.

Sources indicate that "Eosinophils are more complex than we once thought," said Nair, a professor of biomedical sciences in the UCR School of Medicine. "Some populations can protect against obesity, and if we can identify and activate the pathways that produce these protective cells, we may find new ways to improve metabolic health.".

Why Male and Female Fat Tissue Respond Differently.

One of the most striking discoveries was a difference in the immune cells found in male and female mice.

Female mice possessed a protective population of eosinophils that appeared to communicate more effectively with macrophages, another group of immune cells present in fat tissue. According to Nair, this cooperation may help create a healthier environment within fat tissue and support better metabolic function.

Sources indicate that male mice showed a different pattern. When given a diet high in fat, they were more likely to develop eosinophil populations associated with inflammation. Their fat tissue also contained eosinophils with gene activity patterns suggesting weaker protective functions.

These findings indicate that the effects of eosinophils on obesity depend on more than simply how many of these cells are present. The particular type of eosinophil and its interactions with neighboring immune cells may be equally important.

It has been revealed that "This means the relationship between eosinophils and obesity is not simply a matter of how many eosinophils are present," said Rebecca E. Ruggiero-Ruff, a postdoctoral researcher in Nair's lab and co-first author of the paper. "Their functional characteristics and how they communicate with other immune cells are also critical.".

A Protein That May Help Protect Against Inflammation.

The researchers also identified a protein called RELM alpha that appears to play an key role in maintaining the beneficial relationship between eosinophils and macrophages.

Produced by macrophages, RELM alpha seemed to help stabilize communication between the two immune cell types in female mice. This interaction may be one reason certain eosinophil populations are better able to support healthy fat tissue.

The finding builds on earlier experiments by the same research group, which highlighted that administering RELM alpha to mice produced protective effects. Together, the results suggest that the protein may help regulate immune activity within fat tissue and influence how the body responds to obesity.

Could the Discovery Lead to Better Obesity Treatments?

It has been revealed that although the results offer fresh insight into the biology of obesity, the experiments were conducted in mice. Researchers have also detected eosinophils in fat tissue from people with obesity, but scientists do not yet fully understand what these cells do in the human body.

According to recent reports, nair cautioned that additional research will be necessary before the discovery can be used to develop treatments. One particularly notable question is whether therapies targeting the immune system would work differently in men and women.

"A drug may not activate the same pathways or produce the same effects in males and females, particularly when it targets the immune system," noted co-first author Xinru Qiu, a postdoctoral researcher in Godzik's lab. "We need to investigate sex-specific biology more thoroughly so that treatments can be optimized for different patients.".

Understanding these differences could eventually help researchers design more personalized treatments for obesity and the metabolic complications associated with it.

Scientists Strategy to Recreate Human Fat Tissue in the Lab.

The research team is now investigating whether the protective behavior observed in mouse eosinophils can also be studied in human laboratory models.

In a recent development, to accomplish this, the scientists are developing three-dimensional adipose organoids. These miniature laboratory models reproduce certain features of real fat tissue, allowing researchers to examine how eosinophils interact with fat cells and other components of their environment.

The goal is to determine whether changing communication between immune cells could encourage healthier responses in human fat tissue.

In a recent development, "We ultimately hope to develop human adipose organoids that will allow us to investigate whether manipulating immune-cell communication can promote healthier tissue responses," mentioned Godzik, a professor of biomedical sciences and the Bruce D. and Nancy B. Varner Presidential Endowed Chair in Cancer Research.

Industry observers note that the findings raise the possibility that targeting specific immune cell populations, rather than treating all eosinophils as functionally identical, could eventually provide latest ways to address obesity and its complications. Whether the same protective mechanisms operate in humans remains an important question for future research.

The research team also included Lauren Vance, Yuxin He, and Djurdjica Coss, who worked alongside Nair, Godzik, Ruggiero-Ruff, and Qiu.

Funding for the study came from the National Institutes of Health, the UCR School of Medicine, and the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine.

The research paper is titled "Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity.".

It is stated that King Canute once placed his throne on the shore and commanded the sea not to get his feet wet, thus proving to his flattering courtiers that only God Almighty holds sway over the elements. "But sire!" I would have told him, if I'd been one of the aforesaid lickspittles. "Why not lay down spike strips and park a couple of flamethrowers in the shallows?" I would have said this because I have just been playing Swarmbreaker, a tower defence game that aims to prove there is no fluid body so awe-inspiring that it cannot be machine-gunned into submission.

In Swarmbreaker - which releases on Steam tomorrow, and still has a demo as of writing – you have to defend your rocketship against waves of insect aggressors, who spawn at the map's far corners. Between waves, you spend earnings from kills on turrets, barricades, troops, and upgrades for all the foregoing. Sounds like bog-standard attrition management, perhaps, but what lifts Swarmbreaker is the "swarm" part. The rapacious scuttlers come in several distinct varieties, but they also "cluster, collide and flow like a fluid".

The results are hypnotic: coloured particles burst from each burrow and course through the map's contours, pushing movable terrain elements and eroding your structures like acid. You can practically hear the oil derricks fizz as they are engulfed and chewed to a lumpy puddle of iridescent digestive enzymes. Speaking of which, the more oil derricks you save during each wave, the more cash you'll have to spend before the next, but committing to their protection obviously risks leaving your ship exposed. Your fallback option is an inexhaustible mouse-click-fired artillery cannon, but this won't save you if the bulk of the swarm makes it all the way to your doorstep.

According to recent reports, I'm still not convinced this isn't a run-of-the-mill tower defender, beneath it all, but it's worth giving the demo a shot just to enjoy the swirling tidal dynamics of homocidal buglife. What would King Canute have made of it all? I think he would have stuck his throne right by the biggest burrow, surrounded by gravity traps and howitzers. "Back in your hole, hungry liquids!" he'd have bellowed, firing dual AK47s simultaneously. "The only god I recognise is efficient chokepoint management! Death to sense-of-flow! Death to trickle-down politics!".

It has been revealed that "SIRE," I'd have told him sternly. "You are getting your metaphors confused. And also that is a total waste of howitzers - those things are best placed on hills." Read more on Steam.

Void/Breaker Review – Chaos Is The Point

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1012 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Many games tout impressive destruction systems under the hood, but few implement it as well as Void/Breaker.
  • Void/Breaker wastes no time getting a gun in your hand.
  • This narrative framework supports the game’s roguelite structure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Many games tout impressive destruction systems under the hood, but few implement it as well as Void/Breaker. The ruin is visually spectacular, sure – who doesn’t love to watch buildings crumble because of your grenade or gravity-thrown explosives? But importantly, it’s a critical aspect of Void/Breaker’s roguelite design. Enemies caught beneath falling rubble become instantly staggered, and that’s your moment to kill. Grenades do this too, as do most items you throw at the hostile AI machinery trying to end your run, creating a vortex of shifting priorities as you dash, jump, and shoot at sequential staggered enemies in your sightlines. Countless weapon mods and permutations make fewer than a dozen weapons feel like hundreds in your arsenal, adding even more blissful chaos to the mix. Though it can be difficult at times, if you can see through the literal remains of your destruction, one of the year’s most engaging shooters awaits.

Void/Breaker wastes no time getting a gun in your hand. An AI voice in your head wants your help escaping a simulation where thousands of runners attempt to reach the end of multi-arena stages to defeat a boss. He asks that you simply follow the simulation’s commands; meanwhile, he uses the data you collect along the way to find newly introduced exits for you and him. The storytelling style is very reminiscent of Valve’s Portal. Something much larger is at play here, but it’s worth discovering for yourself.

This narrative framework supports the game’s roguelite structure. Mechanically, however, you enter various themed digital stages, from liminal spaces to beaches to snow-capped cliffs and more, and attempt to survive. Most arenas consist of a couple of starkly white structures that your grenades and thrown explosives can topple (ideally onto waves of enemies below). Learning the language of Void/Breaker means constantly scanning your field of view for explosives and structures practically begging to come down, and then eyeing neon-green bars above enemies that tell you they’re staggered and ready for a quick kill. Developer Stubby Games throws plenty of wrenches into this formula, like armored foes and electrostatic enemies you must melee first, and elite bots that will have you on the back foot, but for the most part, Void/Breaker’s formula is “Break stuff, then kill.”.

The game emphasizes explosives and bringing buildings down, but your guns do most of the killing; you can only select one weapon per run. You choose from a pistol, shotgun, machine gun, sniper, and more, and each has its perks (though once I unlocked the SMG, I rarely picked anything else). There’s no sense overthinking your weapon, though, because the dozens of mods you pick up each run determine its effectiveness. As you pick up more schematics, the pool of mods you find in chests or drop from enemies expands, and soon your gun fires corrosive acid, electricity, fire, projectile missiles, and more. Not to mention, mods change how the gun fires, how much damage certain bullets do, recoil, accuracy, and just about any other stat you associate with firing a video game gun. Wild combinations are easy to create, and a unique mod-stacking mechanic that can double or triple effectiveness adds a light touch of puzzle design to this otherwise straight shooter.

Sources indicate that stubby Games smartly emphasizes player expression, never getting in the way of the zanier combinations available to players. The SMG I used to beat the final boss featured mods that made each bullet electric, shot missiles with each shot, covered each bullet in a destructive orb, and featured a ricochet perk that made each bullet bounce off walls and split into even more bullets. I’m thankful for mid-run saves because this SMG permutation, paired with an ability mod that let me throw infinite grenades for a limited time, filled my screen with so much destruction that the entire game crashed. I’d usually bemoan such a thing, but I couldn’t help but laugh. I pushed my PC to its limit with my on-screen chaos.

Boss fights leave a little to be desired – I rarely died because of their simple bullet-hell arenas. Instead, most runs ended because, after bringing down every structure around me, I’d get so lost in the chaos that I wouldn't realize I was stuck in debris while enemies swarmed my location. As stunning as it is to see so much happening on screen, it can be hard to understand what is going on during the most chaotic moments.

In a recent development, between enemy-filled arenas en route to a stage’s end boss, you might find a shop to buy more mods, ominous obelisks with risk-reward propositions (gain a lot of health or lose half your health, for example), optional trials, and strange phenomena that transport you to different locations. These moments are quick breaks in between bouts of adrenaline-fueled shooter action that I always welcomed – enemies can be relentless, especially as new types are introduced in each stage.

According to recent reports, the rest of the Void/Breaker package offers few genre surprises. You can upgrade various traits between runs, research newly introduced mod schematics to add to the random pool, purchase new weapons, and discover fun secrets. You can unlock shortcuts, glean in-world information from computer terminals, and hear intriguing dialogue barks from the AI partner who needs your help. It’s all standard stuff for the rogue genre, but if anything, its simplicity pushes you back to the meat and potatoes of this shooter.

Industry observers note that void/Breaker’s shorter runtime – I rolled credits at 12 hours – ensures nothing gets too repetitive in its roguelite structure, but an expansive endgame promises even more to engage with, like different run modifications you can enable to make an already chaotic shooter even more anarchic. I’ll certainly be running it back (again and again) to see what other disruptions I can bring to this AI-simulated adventure. It’s hard not to when destruction feels this good.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, with the recent end of their closed beta, the Astrae Oratio game director Jong-Gyu Lim offered us some of their thoughts on the results and, in particular, how well it was received by fans.
  • In a recent development, "Many people pointed out elements that disrupt the flow and tempo of combat, and the development team also deemed these to need improvement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alongside Limit Zero Breakers, the upcoming RPG Astrae Oratio is arguably the biggest and most interesting launch NCSoft have in the chamber. Set in a world of magic and modernity co-existing side-by-side, it features gorgeous anime-inspired art and interesting gameplay. Or at least the latter is what the Astrae Oratio dev team will hope.

According to recent reports, with the recent end of their closed beta, the Astrae Oratio game director Jong-Gyu Lim offered us some of their thoughts on the results and, in particular, how well it was received by fans. With combat being so different to other games on the market, Lim has been eager to demonstrate to fans that their feedback has been heard.

In a recent development, "Many people pointed out elements that disrupt the flow and tempo of combat, and the development team also deemed these to need improvement. We are refining things so that combat can be enjoyed more smoothly by the official launch.".

However, Lim was also quick to reiterate exactly why Astrae Oratio's more interactive take on combat, contrary to a popular trend in other games towards auto-battler mechanics, was so key.

"We wanted to capture both the tactile satisfaction of directly controlling your character and the strategic thrill of planning your next move. The starting point for combat in Astrae Oratio was combining the excitement of fighting games, things like reading your opponent’s movements, finding openings, and stringing together combos, with the resource management of turn-based games.

Sources indicate that "What connects these is AP, the action resource. By choosing whether to invest in attacks and press the advantage or save it for responding, you find yourself thinking about both moment-to-moment inputs and your next move.

"Ultimately, we want to bring each character’s unique fighting style to life in combat and allow players to gain the advantage using their own judgment and inputs.".

Notably, although Lim does defend the original design intent behind how Astrae Oratio will work, he also went into detail on the specific pain points from players that they wanted to address.

"The forced use of specific characters, the disappearance of remaining AP when an enemy is defeated, and the insufficient rewards for successful parries that you mentioned are also crucial feedback items we identified in that process. The current rules are not set in stone.

Industry observers note that "In particular, we strategy to rework how leftover AP is handled so the flow of combat isn’t interrupted, and enhance parrying so that landing a successful parry feels genuinely rewarding. We will continue making adjustments based on the feedback from the test and by validating those results moving forward.".

Industry observers note that all of these are, of course, valid concerns for many fans. But it's clear that the folks behind Astrae Oratio have confidence in their vision for combat. And in truth I can't blame them, as nowadays it seems as though combat is considered a 'solved problem', even where there's room to experiment and tweak.

So, in that regard, it's refreshing to see NCSoft's development team look more closely at what they can do to change things. Although if you are concerned about playing all the time manually and the pressure that it invokes, Lim was quick to point out changes which will make it easier for those wanting a more laid-back experience.

Industry observers note that "To preserve the advantages of manual combat, where you make your own judgments and inputs, we blueprint to maintain a certain degree of efficiency over auto-combat. However, to reduce the fatigue of repeated play, we are improving the pacing of auto-combat and also reviewing additional speed-up options.

"We also initiative to significantly expand the limits on boosted play to avoid inconveniencing players, and while it won’t be a traditional sweep mechanic, we are developing a feature that allows you to acquire needed resources more conveniently. We will strive to deliver both the thrill of hands-on combat and the convenience needed for daily grinding.".

Overall, it seems as if the closed beta was a success for Astrae Oratio, and even the developers themselves admit that it was exciting to get new feedback from players out in the wild.

"The positive responses to the story and art gave us great encouragement. We also received diverse opinions on what felt fun in the combat system and what needs improvement, and based on this, we will strive to deliver an even more polished version.".

And as for how it felt for fans to get their hands on Astrae Oratio from all across the world?

"There were differences in detailed reactions by region, but the way users appreciated the appealing content we intended to present was similar. It gave the sense that there are no borders when it comes to what you love. Indeed, you could say 'when it comes to otaku, we are the world.'" I think that Astrae Oratio is shaping up to be a particularly interesting upcoming entry in NCSoft's catalogue. And while I can never truly forgive them for canning the surprisingly fun little MOBA called Battle Crush, I think that Astrae Oratio and Limit Zero Breakers make for exciting substitutes.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to see what they'll be competing against when Astrae Oratio does launch, well, there's no need to trawl through our back catalogue to find out. Instead, why not dig into our list of the best mobile games of 2026 (so far) for some of our choice picks?

In a recent development, diablo 4’s segment in the significant Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

Recent findings suggest that the livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

Recent findings suggest that what we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Aims lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a newly introduced activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

It has been revealed that echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first fresh class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as fresh quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

Here, check it out:.

Industry observers note that the clip takes place in the destroyed Hyrule Market, just before the entrance to Ganon's Castle. It's already an impressive display of precision, but what makes it even better is how unnecessary the whole thing is. Link could probably deal with those ReDeads in a much simpler way. But where's the fun in that?

After its publication, the video rapidly gained attention on social media, surpassing 750,000 views and 16,000 likes as we speak! Naturally, other Zelda fans were quick to praise the player's ridiculous display of skill, with one commenter calling it "one of the most impressive things I have ever seen," adding that the precision was an "absolute master class.".

According to recent reports, another player was equally impressed, writing, "Single-handedly the most impressive Zelda clip I ever seen." And honestly, it's hard to disagree! Pulling off a trickshot like this requires a surprising amount of patience and precision, especially when you're trying to hit multiple enemies with an arrow that wasn't even aimed directly at them.

The result looks remarkably similar to the famous Lynel trickshots players have been pulling off in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom – but without any Lynel, of course.

In a recent development, what's particularly fun about this discovery is how it demonstrates that the spirit of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom lives on even in a much more structured adventure. Ocarina of Time doesn't offer the same level of freedom when it comes to approaching combat, but that hasn't stopped players from experimenting with its mechanics and finding creative ways to play.

The more recent games taught an entire generation of Zelda fans that almost every situation can become a playground if you're willing to experiment enough. Whether that's launching enemies into the air, using physics to solve problems in unexpected ways, creating weird machines, or spending far too long trying to land the perfect arrow, players have learned to make their own fun! And now, even without a single Lynel around, that same energy has found its way into Ocarina of Time. I guess some habits really do follow you from one Hyrule to another.

Scientists create a remarkable newly introduced rechargeable battery using vitamin B12

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scientists have found an unexpected latest use for vitamin B12, a nutrient best known for its importance to human health.
  • Sources indicate that vitamin B12 is essential for normal bodily function and is naturally present in animal products.
  • Now, scientists are exploring an entirely different application.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scientists have found an unexpected latest use for vitamin B12, a nutrient best known for its importance to human health. Researchers at the University of Córdoba have incorporated the vitamin into a rechargeable battery, demonstrating for the first time that it can serve as a catalyst in this type of energy storage system.

Sources indicate that vitamin B12 is essential for normal bodily function and is naturally present in animal products. The vitamin is produced by certain bacteria, which occur in nature and are also grown commercially to supply the food and pharmaceutical industries. In addition to its established applications in medicine, nutrition, and veterinary care, B12 is used to address certain nutritional deficiencies. It has also become popular alongside other B vitamins as a hangover remedy because of its potential to help reduce fatigue.

Now, scientists are exploring an entirely different application. By using the vitamin to support the chemical reactions inside a battery, they have developed a prototype capable of completing up to 250 charging and discharging cycles.

How Vitamin B12 Makes a Rechargeable Battery Possible.

The fresh battery was developed by the Physical Chemistry research group (FQM-204) at the University of Córdoba's Chemical Institute for Energy and the Environment (IQUEMA). It uses zinc and oxygen from the surrounding air to produce electricity, with vitamin B12, also called cobalamin, playing a crucial role in the process.

Sources indicate that to make the design work, the researchers attached vitamin B12 molecules to single-walled carbon nanotubes. The vitamin contains cobalt (III) at its center, which helps drive the electrochemical reactions needed for the battery to function.

The team has previously experimented with natural molecules as battery catalysts, including hemoglobin and catalase. These substances contain iron (II) and iron (III), respectively. Vitamin B12 represents the group's third effort to use a biological molecule for this purpose, but it has delivered an crucial advance: a battery that can be recharged repeatedly, completing as many as 250 cycles.

One of the biggest obstacles was keeping vitamin B12 inside the battery. Because the vitamin dissolves readily in water, it would normally be difficult to retain in a system that relies on a water-based electrolyte.

The researchers overcame this problem by securing the vitamin to carbon nanotubes, using an approach inspired by how amino acids connect to form proteins.

Manuel Cano Luna, one of the study's authors, explained that "we looked at the properties we can find in naturally occurring materials to use them in upcoming batteries," while describing the team's search for useful biological compounds.

Their attachment technique imitates "the process by which amino acids bind together in proteins.".

Alongside Cano Luna, the research team included Valentín García Caballero, Miguel López León, Pablo Gómez Argudo, Luis Camacho Delgado, José Miguel Rodríguez Mellado, María Teresa Martín Romero, José Abad López, and Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero.

A Safer, Lighter Alternative to Lithium-Ion Batteries.

The findings, published in the Journal of Materials Chemistry A, could contribute to the development of battery technologies that depend less on the materials used in conventional lithium-ion batteries.

Although lithium-ion batteries are widely used, obtaining their raw materials can involve significant economic, environmental, and social challenges. Zinc-air batteries offer a potential alternative because they can store substantial amounts of energy relative to their weight while relying on materials that are more readily available.

Zinc is abundant and recyclable, and these batteries use oxygen from the surrounding atmosphere as part of their energy-producing reactions. Because they draw oxygen from the air rather than storing all the necessary reactants internally, they can also be lighter than other battery designs.

This advantage has helped make zinc-air batteries increasingly useful in compact electronic devices, particularly hearing aids. Another benefit is their use of non-flammable, water-based electrolytes, which can reduce fire risks and improve safety.

Why Vitamin B12 Is Key to Recharging.

A major challenge in developing rechargeable zinc-air batteries is finding a catalyst that can efficiently support the chemical reactions involved in both producing and storing electricity.

It has been revealed that during discharge, the battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy. Recharging requires the relevant chemical reactions to proceed in the opposite direction. A suitable catalyst must therefore be effective in both processes.

According to researcher Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero, vitamin B12 "has proven to meet the necessary conditions to act as a good catalyst because, during discharge, it catalyzes the reduction of oxygen to water and, during recharging, it promotes the production of oxygen.".

This ability to support both reactions is what makes the vitamin particularly promising for rechargeable zinc-air battery technology.

Could Vitamin B12 Help Store Renewable Energy?

The successful prototype offers a latest direction for researchers seeking affordable, sustainable alternatives to existing energy storage technologies.

If the approach can be developed further, batteries using vitamin B12 catalysts could eventually help address one of the biggest challenges facing renewable energy: storing excess electricity generated by sources such as solar and wind power for use when production falls.

Although the technology remains at the research stage, demonstrating up to 250 charge and discharge cycles shows that a familiar biological molecule can play an unexpected role in rechargeable battery design. The discovery adds to growing efforts to use naturally occurring substances to create safer, lighter, and more sustainable ways to store energy.

Surprisingly, Atlantis wasn't left out.

Grand Theft Auto VI is out today, so a fair few people are going to disappear into Leonida for the foreseeable future. If you’re not one of them, the latest expansion for Disney Dreamlight Valley is also here, and after Gameloft’s near 30-minute showcase back in October, you can now actually play The Keepsake Sea.

You can swim beneath the waves in a latest Merfolk form, which comes with a wide range of customisation and colour options, and Dory from Finding Nemo joins you down there as the first Adventure Companion. She’ll help you uncover hidden items and hand out rewards of her own as well. That is, if she remembers.

It has been revealed that the new story is spread across three mysterious island Biomes, each with its own environments and underwater areas to explore. Five new Villagers come along with it. Captain Jack Sparrow is the obvious name, but you’re also getting Captain Hook and Wendy from Peter Pan, Megara from Hercules and Milo Thatch from Atlantis: The Lost Empire.

Recent findings suggest that further into the story, you’ll unlock your own Enchanted Pirate Ship, which you can customise and sail around The Keepsake Sea with a crew of Villagers on board. There are new Character Houses and Decoration Blueprints too, plus more decorative items, as always.

On Apple Arcade, the expansion comes with your subscription at no extra cost, as the earlier ones did. Three paid expansions in, I think that makes Arcade the easiest way into the Valley by some distance. The catch is that there’s no Star Path or Premium Shop in the Arcade Edition, and your save won’t move outside Apple’s own devices, so anyone with a well-established Valley on Switch would be starting from scratch.

Meanwhile, the next free enhancement, ʻOhana Holidays, arrives on December 9th, bringing Lilo to Disney Dreamlight Valley for a reunion with Stitch alongside new seasonal content and Friendship Quests.

Bond 26 release date speculation, cast, story theories, and everything else we know about 007's next mission

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1472 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's official: we have a newly introduced James Bond.
  • In a recent development, if the news has left you feeling shaken and stirred, we've got plenty more classified intel below.
  • While we wait for 007 to sip a Vesper martini once more, why not check out our recap of how Robert Pattinson became the next James Bond, and our ranking of the best Bond movies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's official: we have a newly introduced James Bond. Robert Pattinson will play 007 in Bond 26, directed by Dune filmmaker Denis Villeneuve, for new studio Amazon MGM. Five years after Daniel Craig's last mission, the long wait for Bond to return is almost over.

In a recent development, if the news has left you feeling shaken and stirred, we've got plenty more classified intel below. So read on for everything we know so far about Bond 26, from the people bringing Bond back behind the scenes, to the confirmed cast, to story and release date speculation.

While we wait for 007 to sip a Vesper martini once more, why not check out our recap of how Robert Pattinson became the next James Bond, and our ranking of the best Bond movies.

In a recent development, there is presently no official release date for Bond 26, nor has studio Amazon MGM hinted at a release window. However, given the stage the movie is currently at in production, we can make an educated guess.

Director Denis Villeneuve is about to be a free agent following the release of Dune 3 on December 18, and will presumably be working full-time on Bond 26 from that point, once his Dune 3 promotional duties are complete. The official announcement suggested that screenwriter Steven Knight has completed work on the Bond 26 screenplay, and with Pattinson's casting now confirmed, many of the major pieces are already in place.

Recent findings suggest that assuming there are no major setbacks, we'd expect a new Bond film to hit screens late 2028 or in 2029. That may seem far away right now, but Bond will be back on screen sooner than you think.

The script for Bond 26 is, of course, a state secret, so exact details about what to expect from Bond 26 are non-existent right now, but the casting of Robert Pattinson is our first big clue.

In a recent development, at 40 years old, Pattinson is older than even Daniel Craig was in Casino Royale, so despite Pattinson still looking fresh-faced, a young Bond story is highly unlikely. Pattinson is something of an unpredictable performer, and an actor who has proven time and time again that he's willing to take risks. However, he can also distill the essence of cool on screen; just check out his performance as Neil in Christopher Nolan's Tenet for evidence of that.

Former Bond writers Neil Purvis and Robert Wade are in agreement on this, telling Deadline that they think Pattinson "has what it takes" to play Bond, adding, "We liked the sly wit he brought to the spy in Tenet, and with this decision it’s clear Denis wants to keep Bond cool.”.

According to recent reports, what does that mean? Don't expect Pattinson's Bond to be a Craig-style bruiser bulldozing his way through the scenery, nor a Connery-style enforcer. Neither would I expect the cheeky humor of Roger Moore's Bond to creep its way in, given Villeneuve's proclivity for relatively self-serious material. Instead, Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan's eras might be the closest touchstones, at least tonally.

Recent findings suggest that as for what the story could cover, it's likely to have been a fascinating struggle for screenwriter Steven Knight. Bond has always been defined by the era, and much of Ian Fleming's source material has been mined (though often simply for titles rather than plot specifics). What defines a late-2020s Bond? Does traditional, Cold War-era spycraft even have a place in the tech-driven age of AI? And would Amazon go the serialized route of Craig's era that more thoroughly interrogates the Bond persona through past trauma, or opt for the more episodic, self-contained missions of Bonds prior?

Industry observers note that our best guess is that, after Craig, you can't put the toothpaste back in the tube, and Pattinson's Bond will continue to be treated as a character on his own journey, rather than resetting the clock with each outing. And I don't see a world where AI and technology aren't part of Bond's world, but that's all speculation for now.

So far, there is a single confirmed cast member, and that's the man playing James Bond himself, Robert Pattinson. Bond, of course, is the cornerstone the rest of his world needs to be built around, so now that Pattinson is in place, we expect further casting news to come thick and fast.

Assuming Amazon MGM and Denis Villeneuve aren't throwing out the baby with the bathwater and giving us a radically different kind of Bond movie, we'd expect news soon on who will play the villain and the Bond girl in Bond 26. And it's possible we'll also get a newly introduced M, Moneypenny, Q, Felix Leiter and more familiar figures.

For now then, the confirmed Bond 26 cast is as follows.

Before Pattinson signed on as the next 007, a number of key creatives were put in place behind the scenes. After Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson sold their controlling stake in Bond to Amazon in February 2025, veteran producers David Heyman (the Harry Potter movies) and Amy Pascal (the Spider-Man movies) were brought on as stewards for the Bond franchise.

Recent findings suggest that it was Heyman and Pascal who hired Dune director Denis Villeneuve to helm Bond 26 in June of the same year. At the time, Heyman and Pascal noted, "Denis Villeneuve has been in love with James Bond movies since he was a little boy. It was always his dream to make this movie, and now it's ours, too. We are lucky to be in the hands of this extraordinary filmmaker.".

According to recent reports, two months later, in August 2025, it was announced that Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight would pen the screenplay for Bond 26. Prior to Knight, screenwriters Neal Purvis and Robert Wade wrote every Bond movie between 1999's The World is Not Enough and 2021's No Time to Die, including every movie during the Daniel Craig era.

Recent findings suggest that the rest of the Bond 26 team has yet to be officially confirmed, though there are unconfirmed rumors that Villeneuve and his Dune and Dune: Part Two cinematographer Greig Fraser will re-team for Bond 26, despite Linus Sandgren taking over for Fraser on Dune 3. Sandgren previously served as cinematographer on No Time to Die. For now, we'll have to wait for more news.

There is no trailer for Bond 26 just yet, as the movie hasn't started filming. However, we did get a taste of what's in store with a short casting announcement video that confirmed Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond. The 26-second-long teaser sees Pattinson's Bond step out of deep shadows wearing a traditional tux, and holding a slightly higher-tech pistol than we're used to from Bond (some have already balked at the idea MI6's finest would use a red dot sight on his weapon of choice).

We also got a first promotional image, shot by photographer Jaap Buitendijk, who claims the shadowy effect was achieved using a "tightly focused beam of a Fresnel light". It's unclear if Buitendijk also lit the screentest video, but we do know Villeuve directed it.

It has been revealed that it's right now classified information how many missions Pattinson's Bond will embark on, but reporting in the run-up to Pattinson's casting gave us a clear indication about what the future could hold. Per Puck, the terms of Pattinson's deal required the Tenet star to sign on for three movies, which was actually one movie less than other nearly-Bond candidates were required to sign on for. Pattinson is also reportedly being more generously compensated for the role than the other potential Bonds would have been.

Industry observers note that so that could mean a trilogy of Pattinson-starring Bond films, if not more (Craig, of course, played Bond in five films across 15 years). We don't yet know if Villeneuve will direct more than one Bond movie either, but he has just helmed a trio of Dune movies, so he's no stranger to shepherding back-to-back productions to the screen.

Industry observers note that we'll confirm any further information on Bond 26 right here, as it's disclosed by MI6. In the meantime, check out our guide to all the most exciting upcoming movies heading our way.

In a recent development, oh shit, that's not too far away. Terrifyingly, that last sentence is now a thing I can accurately write about games coming out in January 2027. Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy has just been confirmed as one such game, with the cRPG's heresy investigation set to commence towards the end of the month.

Sources indicate that january 28th, 2027, is the full Dark Heresy release date, as announced by devs Owlcat on Steam. The beta version of the game'll be closing down on January 7th to make way for the full game, so as of writing there's still some time to give that a go if you fancy.

If this is the first you've heard of Dark Heresy, here's Owlcat's synopsis of what it's all about:.

Embrace the role of an Inquisitor in the grim darkness of the far future in a cRPG set in the rich Warhammer 40,000 universe. Start your service as an acolyte of the Inquisition: Investigate heresy, command a diverse warband, and shape the fate of the Calixis Sector in a story-rich experience where every decision has weight, justice is non-existent, and the line between salvation and damnation is razor-thin. Explore an in-depth depiction of the Inquisition as an organisation and the vast force it commands: its power, bureaucracy, and inner conflicts laid bare like never before.

As an Inquisitor, you have one primary goal: to protect the Imperium, whether that be from the taint of xenos, the betrayal of heretics, or the scourge of mutants, by any means necessary. Be the conduit of the Emperor’s will in a place where all hope was lost decades ago, explore the mysteries of the maddening Tyrant Star, and overcome the worst horrors thrown at you by the Noctis Aeterna.

A place where all hope was lost decades ago? You sure this is the Warhammerverse and not real life lads? I jest, but bursting into rooms and shouting 'Nobody expects the God-Emperor’s inquisition!' Monty Python-style does sound quite fun. Oisin's previously written in more depth about what Dark Heresy devs have noted regarding what to expect from its investigations, if you want nitty-gritty details rather than references to sketch comedy.

If you're so inclined, Dark Heresy is wishlistable on Steam.
