Industry News: Scientists discover a hidden hereditary form of aggressive prostate cancer

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that scientists have identified a previously unrecognized inherited form of prostate cancer that, although extremely rare, can lead to aggressive disease relatively early in life.
  • Most cancers develop as genetic changes build up in cells over time.
  • Sources indicate that among the most familiar examples are mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that scientists have identified a previously unrecognized inherited form of prostate cancer that, although extremely rare, can lead to aggressive disease relatively early in life. The discovery, made by researchers at the University of British Columbia (UBC), could help doctors identify families with a heightened genetic risk and detect cancer before it spreads.

Most cancers develop as genetic changes build up in cells over time. However, approximately 5% to 10% are associated with inherited mutations that can be passed from parents to their children, creating a cancer risk that may extend across generations.

Sources indicate that among the most familiar examples are mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes. These inherited changes can substantially raise the likelihood of breast, ovarian, pancreatic, and prostate cancers. Testing for BRCA mutations has reshaped cancer prevention and treatment by allowing people with elevated risks to receive earlier screening and preventive care.

Now, a study published in Cancer Discovery points to another gene, CDK12, as a potentially important marker of inherited prostate cancer risk. After examining genetic information from more than 4,500 people with aggressive prostate cancer, the researchers discovered five unrelated men with inherited mutations in CDK12. Every one of these men developed metastatic prostate cancer between ages 44 and 62, meaning the cancer had spread beyond the prostate.

"What's striking is that every patient we identified with this inherited mutation had already developed metastatic disease by the time they were diagnosed," noted senior author Dr. Alexander Wyatt, associate professor of urologic sciences in the UBC faculty of medicine and UBC President's Excellence Chair in Precision Oncology. "The opportunity now is to identify these families earlier and give people the chance to benefit from enhanced screening, when there are still curative treatment options.".

A Hidden Genetic Cause of Aggressive Prostate Cancer.

The discovery challenges a longstanding assumption about CDK12. Scientists previously believed that harmful changes in this gene developed spontaneously inside cancer cells rather than being inherited from a parent.

To investigate whether the inherited mutations were actually contributing to the disease, the team examined the patients' tumors for a distinctive pattern of genetic damage associated with loss of CDK12 function. This molecular fingerprint helped connect the inherited mutations to the development of their cancers.

Sources indicate that "The tumors provided us with a genetic signature that pointed directly back to CDK12," said lead author Dr. Sofie Tolmeijer, a postdoctoral fellow in the Wyatt lab. "It gave us compelling evidence that these inherited mutations were playing a direct role in causing their cancer.".

The findings emerged from a broad international research effort involving UBC, BC Cancer, the Vancouver Coastal Health Research Institute, and the University of Washington, along with scientists at institutions in Australia, the Netherlands, Spain, and Belgium.

Despite the potentially serious consequences, inherited CDK12 mutations appear to be exceptionally uncommon. The researchers found them in approximately one out of every 1,000 people with aggressive prostate cancer. Even at that low frequency, they estimate that hundreds of families around the world could be affected.

"While this mutation is extremely rare, the discovery could be lifesaving for the families who carry it," said Dr. Tolmeijer. "Finding one person with an inherited mutation gives us the opportunity to identify other family members at risk and help them take action before cancer develops or spreads.".

Genetic Testing Could Help Detect Prostate Cancer Earlier.

One of the most promising implications of the discovery is that doctors may not need to develop entirely newly introduced testing technology to put the findings into practice.

The researchers recommend including CDK12 in standard genetic testing panels used to assess hereditary prostate cancer risk. These panels examine multiple genes associated with inherited cancer susceptibility, helping identify individuals who may benefit from closer medical monitoring.

Industry observers note that importantly, the clinical technology required to detect CDK12 mutations already exists. That could make expanding genetic testing relatively straightforward, potentially reducing the time and expense needed to bring the discovery into routine patient care.

"One of the most exciting aspects of this discovery is that we already have the technology needed to act on it," stated Dr. Wyatt, who is also a senior research scientist at the Vancouver Prostate Centre and senior scientist at BC Cancer. "Adding CDK12 to existing genetic tests is relatively straightforward, which means this discovery could move from the research lab into clinical care much more swiftly.".

Could the Same Mutation Increase Ovarian Cancer Risk?

The study also uncovered clues suggesting that inherited CDK12 mutations might be associated with ovarian cancer, although more research is needed to establish whether they increase the risk.

In a recent development, several of the men with inherited CDK12 mutations had relatives with a history of ovarian cancer. The investigators also identified another person who had ovarian cancer and carried an inherited CDK12 mutation. Analysis of that person's tumor revealed the same characteristic genetic signature seen in the prostate cancer cases.

It has been revealed that together, these observations suggest that CDK12 could potentially play a role in hereditary cancer risk beyond the prostate. Further studies will be needed to determine how strongly the mutations are associated with ovarian cancer and whether they should influence screening recommendations.

For families carrying these rare mutations, the potential benefits of identifying their genetic risk could be substantial. Earlier testing may give relatives the opportunity to receive closer surveillance and, if cancer develops, begin treatment before it reaches an advanced stage.

"With the right genetic testing and screening programs, we envision a future where no one who inherits one of these mutations dies from cancer," said Dr. Wyatt.

The research received funding from the Prostate Cancer Foundation, Terry Fox Research Institute, Canadian Cancer Society, Canadian Institutes of Health Research, Michael Smith Health Research BC, U.S. National Institutes of Health, BC Cancer Foundation, and other funding partners.

GTA 6 Breaks a 25-Year Tradition, and Rockstar Explains Why

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (832 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that you can deal drugs, pay for private dances at strip clubs, and even mow down pedestrians in GTA 6.
  • This wasn't simply an overlooked feature.
  • In a recent development, in its response to Shacknews, Rockstar described GTA 6 as a story about a couple on the run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that you can deal drugs, pay for private dances at strip clubs, and even mow down pedestrians in GTA 6. One old activity, though, isn't making the cut. Players can no longer hire sex workers, ending a feature that's been part of the series since Grand Theft Auto 3 arrived in 2001.

This wasn't simply an overlooked feature. Rockstar deliberately left it out. Shacknews asked the GTA studio about it, and they confirmed the feature was removed. Rockstar also offered an explanation, and it comes down to the kind of story it wants to tell with Jason and Lucia.

In a recent development, in its response to Shacknews, Rockstar described GTA 6 as a story about a couple on the run. The studio mentioned it had considered which familiar GTA elements would work alongside the characters and the relationship at the center of the game, rather than bringing back every previous feature by default.

According to recent reports, rockstar pointed to systems such as police pursuits, radio stations, robberies, and car theft as examples of the elements it carried forward. Those all fit the criminal adventures Jason and Lucia get caught up in. Hiring sex workers, apparently, didn't fit what the team had in mind.

According to recent reports, it's an interesting explanation because Rockstar didn't claim the removal was due to a technical limitation or a ratings requirement. Rockstar framed the removal as a creative decision tied to Jason and Lucia's story.

Rockstar framed the removal as a creative decision tied to Jason and Lucia's story.

Anyone who's watched the GTA 6 launch trailer will have seen how much of the marketing revolves around the pair. Rockstar keeps bringing the focus back to Jason and Lucia, even when the trailers show off everything else happening in Leonida. Their story is the reason the two playable protagonists are together in the first place.

According to recent reports, hiring sex workers first became a recognizable open-world interaction in GTA 3, and it remained available across later mainline games, including Vice City, San Andreas, GTA 4, and GTA 5. For some players, it became one of those strange little things they expected to find when wandering around a GTA city at night.

It also brings back one of GTA 3's more infamous controversies. Players could hire a sex worker, kill her afterward, and pick up the money they'd just spent. That drew plenty of criticism at the time, and the mechanic stuck around. It was still possible in GTA 5.

I can't help connecting this to Jason Schreier's 2022 Bloomberg report, which mentioned Rockstar was trying to avoid jokes that punch down at marginalized groups. He suggested GTA 6 might feel quite different from GTA 5, and seeing this particular feature disappear makes me think he might have been onto something. Rockstar says it's about Jason and Lucia, of course, but I wonder if both things played a part.

It was never the reason most people played these games, of course. But GTA has always made a point of filling its streets with activities that aren't strictly necessary for completing missions. The series' reputation comes as much from those distractions as it does from car chases, shootouts, and elaborate heists.

That's why removing a relatively minor interaction is still newsworthy. It has survived several generations of GTA, across different protagonists and settings. Now that Rockstar is putting two characters in a relationship at the heart of its newest game, that particular carryover has finally been dropped.

Recent findings suggest that this doesn't mean GTA 6 has suddenly become a tame version of Grand Theft Auto. The game's nightlife is very much present. Our guide to GTA 6's strip clubs already covers several venues around Leonida, so the absence of one activity shouldn't be confused with the removal of adult entertainment altogether.

It has been revealed that there's a distinction between the atmosphere of Vice City and the specific actions Rockstar lets the protagonists take. A setting can still have strip clubs and the more outrageous side of GTA without including every interaction that existed in previous games.

Industry observers note that the confirmation is also about a specific action players can take. It doesn't establish whether sex workers appear in the game as background characters, or whether the story mentions them. Rockstar answered a question about the gameplay interaction, not every possible appearance of the subject.

Recent findings suggest that some fans will probably find the change strange, particularly if they've been playing since the PS2 days. Others might not have noticed the feature was missing at all. Either way, it's one of the clearer examples of Rockstar choosing to leave an old mechanic behind instead of carrying it over simply because it's always been there.

For a series known for giving players countless ways to get distracted, that's a notable decision. And this time, at least, Rockstar has given a pretty straightforward reason for making it.

#5351. NASA pushes Mars helicopter blades beyond the speed of sound

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1240 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

NASA pushes Mars helicopter blades beyond the speed of sound

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1240 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA is pushing the limits of helicopter flight on Mars, testing rotor blades at speeds once considered too risky.
  • During tests conducted in March at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, engineers successfully pushed the tips of experimental Mars helicopter blades beyond the speed of sound without causing them to break apart.
  • In a recent development, "NASA had a great run with the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, but we are asking these next-generation aircraft to do even more at the Red Planet," said Al Chen, Mars Exploration Program manager at JPL.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA is pushing the limits of helicopter flight on Mars, testing rotor blades at speeds once considered too risky. The faster these blades spin, the more lift they can generate, potentially allowing future aircraft to carry heavier scientific instruments and travel greater distances across the Red Planet.

During tests conducted in March at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, engineers successfully pushed the tips of experimental Mars helicopter blades beyond the speed of sound without causing them to break apart. The experiments took place inside a specialized chamber designed to reproduce the harsh atmospheric conditions on Mars. Results from 137 test runs could help engineers develop a new generation of more powerful aircraft capable of carrying scientific equipment.

In a recent development, "NASA had a great run with the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, but we are asking these next-generation aircraft to do even more at the Red Planet," said Al Chen, Mars Exploration Program manager at JPL. "That's not an easy ask. While everything about Mars is hard, flying there is just about the hardest thing you can do. That's because its atmosphere is so incredibly thin that it is hard to generate lift, and yet Mars has significant gravity.".

Sources indicate that ingenuity made history on April 19, 2021, when it became the first aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another world. However, it was designed primarily to demonstrate that flight on Mars was possible, not to transport scientific instruments. NASA now hopes to go much further. Its recently declared SkyFall project, along with other potential future aircraft, could carry sensors and scientific instruments to investigate Mars from the air. Flying at low altitudes would provide valuable information to support future robotic and human missions.

Why Flying on Mars Requires Extreme Rotor Speeds.

Industry observers note that helicopters generate more thrust by spinning their rotors faster or using blades with a larger diameter. That basic principle applies on Earth and Mars, but the Red Planet presents a much greater engineering challenge.

Mars has an atmosphere only about 1% as dense as Earth's, leaving helicopter blades with far fewer air molecules to push against. To produce enough lift, engineers must operate rotors at exceptionally high speeds, bringing their tips close to the speed of sound. Small rotors on Earth can also spin thousands of times per minute, but the denser atmosphere makes it unnecessary to push their tips toward supersonic speeds to generate substantial lift.

Industry observers note that during Ingenuity's 72 flights on Mars, its engineers limited the helicopter's composite-skinned foam rotors to 2,700 revolutions per minute. This restriction served two crucial purposes. It kept the blades away from the complex and potentially unpredictable conditions near the sound barrier, and it provided a safety margin in case sudden winds (from a dust devil, for instance) caused the blade tips to move faster relative to the surrounding air.

"If Chuck Yeager were here, he'd tell you things can get squirrely around Mach 1," mentioned JPL's Jaakko Karras, the rotor test lead. "With that in mind, we planned Ingenuity's flights to keep the rotor blade tips at Mach 0.7 with no wind so that if we encountered a Martian headwind while in flight, the rotor tips wouldn't go supersonic. But we want more performance from our next-gen Mars aircraft. We needed to know that our rotors could go faster safely.".

The speed of sound also differs considerably between the two planets. At sea level on Earth, Mach 1 is approximately 760 mph (1,223 kph). On Mars, sound travels at roughly 540 mph (869 kph), largely because the atmosphere is much colder and consists primarily of carbon dioxide.

NASA Tests Supersonic Rotors in a Mars Simulation Chamber.

To determine whether the latest blades could safely reach these extreme speeds, Karras and his colleagues used JPL's historic 25-Foot Space Simulator. The rotor systems were developed and manufactured by AeroVironment in Simi Valley, California.

The researchers began with a three-bladed rotor designed for potential future Mars helicopters. After installing it inside the chamber, they removed the surrounding air and introduced a carefully controlled amount of carbon dioxide to recreate the thin Martian atmosphere. They then spun the rotor at progressively higher speeds while exposing it to simulated winds.

In a recent development, because the experiment involved the possibility of a rotor breaking apart at supersonic speeds, engineers reinforced part of the chamber with sheet metal. The team monitored the experiment from a control room located just a few yards away, using instruments and a camera to track the rotor's performance.

Industry observers note that the rotor eventually reached 3,750 revolutions per minute, bringing its blade tips to Mach 0.98, just below the speed of sound. Engineers then switched on a fan to produce headwinds against the spinning blades. With each successive test, they increased the wind speed to push the system further.

Breaking the Sound Barrier Boosts Lift by 30%.

The experiments ultimately drove the rotor tips to Mach 1.08, surpassing the sound barrier and increasing the aircraft's lift capability by 30%. Crucially, the blades survived the supersonic conditions.

Sources indicate that that additional lift could make a major difference for future missions. More powerful Mars helicopters could transport heavier scientific instruments, advanced sensors, and larger batteries, allowing them to conduct more ambitious investigations and remain airborne for longer periods.

Following the successful tests of the three-bladed design, the team evaluated a second rotor intended for SkyFall. This version has two blades that are slightly longer than those used in the first configuration. Because of their greater length, the blade tips could reach the same near-supersonic speed at a lower rotational rate of 3,570 revolutions per minute before simulated headwinds were introduced.

It has been revealed that "The successful testing of these rotors was a major step toward proving the feasibility of flight in more demanding environments, which is key for next-gen vehicles," stated Shannah Withrow-Maser, an aerodynamicist from NASA's Ames Research Center in Silicon Valley and member of the test team. "We thought we'd be lucky to hit Mach 1.05, and we reached Mach 1.08 on our last runs. We're still digging into the data, and there may be even more thrust on the table. These next-gen helicopters are going to be amazing.".

Next-Generation Mars Helicopters Could Launch in 2028.

In a recent development, engineers working on SkyFall have already incorporated the fresh test results into the project's performance specifications. The findings provide an vital foundation for designing helicopters that can operate under more demanding conditions while carrying substantially more equipment than Ingenuity.

Inspired by the historic success of Ingenuity, which remains the only rotorcraft ever to fly on another planet, SkyFall is designed to transport three next-generation helicopters to Mars in December 2028.

If successfully developed and deployed, these aircraft could expand the possibilities for exploring Mars, providing scientists with a newly introduced way to investigate the planet's surface and gather information from locations that may be difficult for traditional rovers to reach.

Materials provided by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, ubisoft has been slowly rolling out mass layoffs since its big restructure earlier this year, and its latest will directly affect the studios responsible for games like Assassin's Creed and Far Cry.
  • "Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," the tech giant claims in a statement provided to IGN and other outlets.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ubisoft has been slowly rolling out mass layoffs since its big restructure earlier this year, and its latest will directly affect the studios responsible for games like Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. Well over 100 developers will lose their jobs at Ubisoft Montréal and Ubisoft Québec.

"Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," the tech giant claims in a statement provided to IGN and other outlets. "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

The company's statement does not specify which projects are affected by the layoffs, though IGN reports that the layoffs primarily affect employees who'd been working on canceled or reworked games. (Both GamesIndustry.biz and VGC offer near-identical background reporting on the nature of the layoffs.).

The Montréal studio has been around since 1997, and is one of the publisher's flagship development houses, leading development on the Splinter Cell, Prince of Persia, Far Cry, and Assassin's Creed franchises over the years. It's now leading development on Assassin's Creed Hexe. Ubisoft Québec has similarly led many Assassin's Creed titles, including Odyssey and Shadows.

According to recent reports, both offices are now part of Vantage Studios, a Tencent-backed subsidiary focused on developing games in the Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and Rainbow Six series. Some of Ubisoft's Montréal operation is now also part of Massive Entertainment, which primarily handles Tom Clancy-branded titles, including The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognize the impact this may have on our colleagues," Ubisoft's statement concludes. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

After laying off thousands, Ubisoft says losing "key talents and skills" is a big danger for the company.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nioh 3 has received a hot new enhancement that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific complications, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest patch, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for patch 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

Recent findings suggest that this is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an concern that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s revision takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an concern that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

#5348. Antarctica’s ice cliffs are collapsing faster than expected, but there’s a twist

Antarctica’s ice cliffs are collapsing faster than expected, but there’s a twist

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1567 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as temperatures rise, the floating ice shelves that help hold Antarctica's massive ice sheet in place are melting and breaking apart at record rates.
  • For years, scientists have believed that ice cliffs become unstable once they exceed 100 meters in height, roughly as tall as the Statue of Liberty.
  • Recent findings suggest that but fresh research from MIT and the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) challenges this long-standing assumption.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as temperatures rise, the floating ice shelves that help hold Antarctica's massive ice sheet in place are melting and breaking apart at record rates. As these protective barriers disappear, they expose towering walls of solid ice. Whether these cliffs remain standing or collapse could play a major role in Antarctica's future ice loss and its contribution to rising sea levels worldwide.

For years, scientists have believed that ice cliffs become unstable once they exceed 100 meters in height, roughly as tall as the Statue of Liberty. According to this theory, a cliff that grows too tall will collapse under its own weight, exposing an even taller wall of ice farther inland. That latest cliff would then collapse, potentially setting off a chain reaction that causes the ice sheet to retreat rapidly.

Recent findings suggest that but fresh research from MIT and the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) challenges this long-standing assumption. The findings suggest that the fate of an Antarctic ice cliff depends on much more than its height, and that even dramatic collapses do not necessarily lead to an unstoppable retreat.

Industry observers note that published in the journal Science, the study examined satellite observations of more than 15,000 Antarctic ice cliffs collected over four years. Researchers discovered a surprising pattern: When the cliffs collapsed, they sometimes retreated much faster than existing models predicted. Yet rather than continuing to disintegrate, the affected glaciers soon stabilized.

"We found that when the cliffs were retreating, they were doing so faster than what has been modeled, which would mean more ice loss and higher contributions of sea level rise," states study author Caroline Needell, a graduate student in the MIT-WHOI Joint Program. "But because we found that the retreat was short-lived, and all the glaciers eventually stabilized, that would suggest that things won't be so bad. We don't see this runaway effect.".

The study's co-authors are Catherine Walker, an assistant scientist at WHOI, and Jeremy Bassis, an associate professor at the University of Michigan.

Why Scientists Expected Antarctica's Ice Cliffs to Collapse.

The possibility of runaway ice cliff collapse is described by a theory called marine ice cliff instability (MICI). It proposes that when an exposed ice wall reaches a critical height, its own weight makes it structurally unstable. If the cliff falls and reveals an even taller wall behind it, the process could repeat, progressively eating away at the Antarctic ice sheet.

Earlier research investigated this possibility primarily through computer models. Scientists used the physical properties of ice to estimate how enormous frozen cliffs should behave, then compared those calculations with a limited number of observations from Antarctica. These studies suggested that cliffs taller than approximately 100 meters were particularly vulnerable to collapse.

"Predictive ice-sheet models that have been used so far to represent ice cliff instability just take into account cliff height," Needell notes. "That's the only variable that matters. And once the cliff height reaches the critical threshold, usually 100 meters, it should initiate this runaway effect of ice sheet retreat.".

Needell and her colleagues wanted to test those predictions against a much larger collection of real-world measurements. They sought to determine how tall Antarctica's ice cliffs actually become and whether their collapse consistently triggers the destructive chain reactions predicted by existing models.

Satellites Reveal Surprising Ice Cliff Stability.

According to recent reports, to investigate, the researchers turned to NASA's Ice, Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2). This spacecraft repeatedly travels over Earth's polar regions, using a laser-based instrument called an altimeter to measure elevations with great precision. Its observations track the heights of glaciers, ice sheets, and sea ice, as well as ocean levels in and around Antarctica.

Recent findings suggest that the team analyzed measurements gathered between 2019 and 2023, examining more than 15,000 ice cliffs at three-month intervals. Most were far shorter than the height considered dangerous by earlier models. The average cliff stood approximately 30 meters tall, although a small number exceeded the proposed 100-meter instability threshold.

The researchers also searched for characteristics that might explain why some cliffs remained stable while others retreated.

It has been revealed that one crucial clue came from the broken ice accumulating in front of the cliffs. Known as mélange, this material consists of a slushy mixture of sea ice and fragments of icebergs. Cliffs that remained relatively stationary tended to have thicker accumulations of mélange, suggesting that the debris could help support the towering ice walls.

"We measured mélange height and found taller cliffs have thicker mélange, which could be a built-in stabilizing effect," Needell explains.

Surrounding seawater provided another possible source of stability. The observations indicated that deeper water can exert greater supporting pressure against an ice cliff, helping counteract the forces that might otherwise cause it to collapse.

Industry observers note that together, these findings suggest that the stability of Antarctica's ice cliffs cannot be predicted by height alone. Conditions in the water surrounding the ice may also determine whether a cliff remains standing.

Antarctica's Tallest Ice Cliffs Collapse, Then Stabilize.

"After we did that global analysis, we thought, ok, let's zoom in on the tallest cliffs and see how they're behaving," Needell claims.

The researchers selected four locations around Antarctica where satellites had recorded some of the tallest ice cliffs. Each stood approximately 100 meters high, with the tallest reaching 127 meters. The team then reconstructed how these cliffs changed at three-month intervals throughout the four-year study.

It has been revealed that the results initially appeared to support the idea that extremely tall cliffs are unstable. These towering walls did collapse, and the glaciers behind them retreated at speeds substantially greater than those anticipated by existing MICI models.

However, the retreat did not continue indefinitely.

"But that retreat was short-lived," Needell notes.

Instead of retreating farther inland in a continuous series of collapses, the glaciers stabilized and eventually advanced outward toward the ocean again.

Industry observers note that "It's this rapid retreat, punctuated by periods of stabilization," Needell says. "That was puzzling to us. Then, we thought: We need to look at all the things that affect cliff height.".

The unexpected pattern suggested that some overlooked physical processes were interrupting the collapse before it could develop into a sustained chain reaction.

Hidden Ridges Beneath the Ice Act as Natural Speed Bumps.

To understand what was stopping the retreat, the team examined the shape of the land beneath Antarctica's ice sheet.

It has been revealed that this underlying terrain, known as bed topography, can strongly influence the height and stability of the ice above it. When the ground is relatively flat, the visible slope of the ice more closely reflects the thickness of the ice itself. But when the terrain rises into a ridge or bump, the ice resting on that elevated ground is thinner than its overall surface elevation might suggest.

These buried rises can function like natural speed bumps. By reducing the thickness of the overlying ice, they can make exposed cliffs shorter and less vulnerable to collapse.

When the scientists compared the locations of stabilizing ice cliffs with measurements of Antarctica's underlying terrain, they found that the cliffs frequently stopped retreating where the ground rose beneath them.

The researchers identified another crucial process. Taller cliffs tended to "thin out" more rapidly as they collapsed. Rather than remaining towering, unstable walls, they could rapidly shrink into shorter cliffs that were better able to withstand further collapse.

These effects help explain why the researchers observed rapid initial ice loss followed by periods of stability, rather than the continuous retreat anticipated by earlier models.

What the Discovery Means for Future Sea Level Rise.

The findings could help scientists improve predictions of how Antarctica's ice sheet will respond to continued warming.

It has been revealed that although the researchers observed some cliffs collapsing faster than expected, the rapid retreat was temporary in the locations they studied. This challenges the assumption that crossing a particular height threshold inevitably leads to runaway collapse.

The results do not mean Antarctica's ice sheet is safe from further losses. Instead, they reveal that predicting its future requires accounting for several interacting factors, including the shape of the land beneath the ice, the rate at which ice becomes thinner, the depth of surrounding water, and the stabilizing effects of broken ice.

Sources indicate that "Now we know what to look for," Needell states. "We really need to know the bed topography, and we need to know the ice thinning rate, in order to get ice cliff instability right, because this value really matters in the context of projecting sea level rise.".

By incorporating these additional processes into ice sheet models, scientists may be able to produce more reliable estimates of Antarctica's future contribution to global sea level rise.

The research received partial support from NASA, the U.S. National Science Foundation, and the DOMINOS project, which is part of the International Thwaites Glacier Collaboration.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it's all or nothing in Outfit7's latest patch for Talking Tom Gold Run, where the concept of "high risk, high return" has never been truer! In particular, a latest Extraction Mode within the endless runner tasks you with running faster and faster for better and better rewards - the catch is that when you crash and burn, so does your hard-earned haul.

Sources indicate that the limited-time event not only challenges your quick reflexes but also your prudence - do you go for the bigger pay-off or leave while you can with what you already have? There are three chances for you to tap out, and once you reach each extraction point, you get to choose whether or not you want to stick around.

It has been revealed that the thing is, if you choose to keep going, the faster the run gets, making obstacles trickier to dodge. Wacky Planet's fast-paced side world offers a little bit of mercy as an indicator tells you how far the next extraction point is - but even so, the gold bars, character cards, and diamonds (which appear later in the run) might just get farther out of reach too.

Industry observers note that there's a handy Save Me option you can opt for when you fail, giving you a chance to revive and continue your run. It's a true test of tapping talent, so it's only fitting you get four new outfits to go along with it!

Tang Suit Ginger, Mooncake Ginger, Moonlight Angela and Hanfu Angela join in to spice up the theming, so if you'd like to look the part while dashing through the upcoming mode, now's your chance.

If you're all set to win big or lose it all, Talking Tom Gold Run's latest event is now live on iOS and Android, and you can download the endless runner for free to get started!

Don't be fooled by Horses of Hoofprint Bay's hand-drawn art, this stable management game has all the drama of a Jilly Cooper novel

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • She was my first horse and she's a competition winner, but she's reached her potential.
  • For all its hand-drawn aesthetics, Horses of Hoofprint Bay has hard realities like the limits of Poema's future bubbling under its surface.
  • There may be better author comparisons, but I learned everything I know about showjumping from Cooper's Riders – much as I learned everything about independent television franchise bids in the '80s from its sequel Rivals – a book which is as much about the nitty gritty of horsetraining and competing as it is about toffs jumping into bed with one another.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Poema is my pride and joy. She was my first horse and she's a competition winner, but she's reached her potential. She'll never be a show jumper, and that's where the money and prestige are to be found. If I'm ever to grow my horse farm into a nationally renowned equestrian centre, I need the cash to expand and upgrade my facilities. Poema is a hoofstep on the path to that future, but she's not going to be able to take me all the way herself.

For all its hand-drawn aesthetics, Horses of Hoofprint Bay has hard realities like the limits of Poema's future bubbling under its surface. While the game's scripted narrative may be lacking, it's shockingly easy to fill in the gaps with drama worthy of a Jilly Cooper novel.

There may be better author comparisons, but I learned everything I know about showjumping from Cooper's Riders – much as I learned everything about independent television franchise bids in the '80s from its sequel Rivals – a book which is as much about the nitty gritty of horsetraining and competing as it is about toffs jumping into bed with one another. In my mind the two are tightly connected - showjumping and Jilly Cooper, not horses and toff bonking. In Horses of Hoofprint Bay, the only real story you get is the fact you've scrimped and saved to buy your first horse and your uncle has lent you the use of his field while you start your business. I was hoping there would at least be a similar setup to Regency Solitaire, where your motivation for touring the country's tearooms is motivated by paying off your brother's gambling debts. Yet, despite this disappointing start, I soon found its business simulation mechanics provide great storytelling material.

Horses of Hoofprint Bay has many of the trappings of a cosy game. At the start of each day, you'll prepare the stables, dragging a rake around the yard to sling away the manure, clicking buckets of water to refill the trough, and making sure there's enough hay for all the horses. But this isn't just for the larks, if you skip these tasks there are serious knock on effects for yours horses. Forget to brush down your horses' coats or pick out the stones in their shoes, and they're liable to develop saddle sores and other injuries when you ride them. Leave an abrasion untreated and it can develop into an infection. Even something like taking a dirty horse to a contest can cost you. I forgot to brush Poema before entering her into her first contest and despite taking first place, her embarrassingly unkempt coat lost my stable prestige. It was a cruel end to what should have been a great celebration.

Sources indicate that so long as your horses are well rested, you can train them each day. You may want to take them through some confidence building lunges, where they need to walk, trot, and canter on demand, or a more physically demanding Cavaletti or showjumping course. These latter too are much more tiring, but they build a horse's strength and endurance. The higher its endurance the more energy it can expend on training sessions each day, and the higher its strength the more jumps it can do in succession before slowing to a walk for a breather - essential when you're competing in a timed competition. Overdo the exercise, however, and you'll exhaust a horse, severely reducing its energy for the next day.

Now, unlike Poema, my freshly bought stallion Kolizey has the potential to compete in showjumping competitions. He'll never go all the way to the big national contests, but he can take a ribbon in the district and regional contests. Or he will when he's up to standard; he's arrived from the breeder in a sorry state: brambles in his mane, mud on his flanks, stones in his shoes, and his strength and endurance are far too low to make it through an entire course of obstacles.

According to recent reports, the biggest problem, however, is Kolizey's confidence: it's shot. I don't know what was happening in the stalls at the breeder's, but he arrived at my stables backing up at the first sign of a jump. Before I can hope to earn him his first ribbon, I have to build up our relationship. If we exercise together enough in the yard, his confidence will grow and he will follow my direction without question.

It may be getting ahead of myself, but I also have intends for Kolizey and Poema to produce a foal. Done right, the two should raise a horse that's able to exceed its parents' potential, becoming stronger and more endurant than both of them. A stronger horse means a ticket to the bigger contests and the bigger prize pots. Not that I can start breeding the two just yet. I want both horses to be at peak physical fitness. Poema's already there, while Kolizey can't even manage a jump without shying away.

While getting Koliszey contest ready, I still need to be bringing in cash. That means using Poema as a training horse for students' riding lessons. The better I am at the minigame where I use the Q, E, W, A, S, and D keys to tell them to sit forward or back, hold the reins higher or lower, or to level out their legs, the more they tip me. I have to be careful, because when Poema is working with students, she's not being stretched, and her strength and endurance can wither which means she struggles to maintain her winning streak in the contests.

Industry observers note that another reason to hold off on getting Poema pregnant is that during the second half of her pregnancy, she can't be ridden, which means no contests and no lessons for students. Presently, those are my two main sources of income besides what I'm paid in rent to board a couple of nearby farmers' horses. I don't want her out of the rota when Kolizey isn't yet ready to step into her place.

According to recent reports, and, well, while I'm on the subject of prepares, reader, I must tell you, the future lies in semen. If I can build the facilities, earn the cash, and raise Kolizey's profile, I can make a good buck on his virile stallion cream. With the money I bring in from a prizewinning semen I can expand into the far field, creating space to take on more horses, upgrade my home from the caravan I'm living in currently, maybe even build a proper training school. I'm not going to afford all that by giving riding lessons to the local children or boarders' rent. No, the big money comes from competition wins and valuable horse sauce.

In a recent development, while Poema continues entering contests and carrying students, I start pushing Kolizey harder. Multiple training sessions every day. I begin with Cavaletti, which is a kind of obedience competition. Your horse has to be travelling at the correct speed when it passes marker flags – walking, trotting, or cantering – and make some small jumps over cross bars. It should be straightforward, but because Kolizey's confidence is so low, he keeps refusing my orders and trying to change speed. He warns me before he's about to speed up or slow down, and if I counter it in time he will obey me and even receive a little confidence boost, but often he does it just before a jump, messing up my timing and he hits the bars. Each time he fails a jump it knocks his confidence, risking me taking me even further from where I need him to be.

In a recent development, I try the easier lunges sessions. And they raise his confidence a little but they're doing little for his physical health. It's all taking too long and Poema's getting older every day. In a fit of frustration, and in mark that I may not be able to cut it as an animal trainer, I skip from the Cavaletti training straight into a showjumping qualifier. The time limits on these are much stricter, so you have to clear the course at a gallop. This is also where a horse's strength really comes into play. The faster you're going, the more strength it requires to jump an obstacle. Horses only recover strength when moving at a walk, so you don't want to tire a horse out by going at a gallop through the whole course, else they won't have the strength to make all the jumps and they'll be forced to withdraw from the event. But nor do you want to go too slowly and fall foul of the time limit.

I realise my mistake as soon as the course begins: I try to stir Kolizey into a walk he refuses. Thankfully the timer only starts when he crosses the line, but it's an inauspicious start. I tap forward again and he begins to walk. I tap again and Kolizey moves up to a trot, then to a canter, before picking up to a gallop. I think he's going too fast as we approach the first jump, but Kolizey clears it. Then another jump and another. With a nervous eye on the depleting strength bar, I tap him down to a canter for the next jump. We're halfway through the course, I briefly slow to a walk to recover some strength then take the next three jumps at a canter. We're so close to the end now but a big yellow exclamation mark appears next to the strength bar. Kolizey is on the edge of exhaustion but he refuses to slow down and increases to a gallop for the last two jumps.

He completes the course with a perfect clear. Not a single obstacle clipped and we end with ten seconds left on the timer. Not only has Kolizey earned his showjumping license, his success swells his confidence. He's a natural athlete.

According to recent reports, the next day, with my horses rested, I take Kolizey and Poema to town to compete in the showjumping and Caprilli events respectively. They both bring home first place, raising the prestige of my stables, earning me a tidy little packet, and convincing me it's time my prized horses started a family. I'm perhaps too eager, when I try to send them to the breeding station, I'm told they're both 'Done for the day'. I suppose I should give my contest winners a bit of a break. They've earned it. I groom them and send them both to bed with an apple as a treat.

It has been revealed that except, maybe they weren't too tired: the next morning, I'm met with a message telling me Poema is pregnant. My stable's become the Olympic Village, with my rosette-winning horses working out the highs and stresses of competition in the only way they know how. Good on them. I needn't have even made the breeding station.

Recent findings suggest that then, with horror, I remember the horses I'm boarding for the neighbours. They're both stallions themselves. Neither of them are at competition level, their strength and endurance is lower even than Poema's when she arrived at the stable. If either of them are the father, Poema is about to be out of action for a whole season and at the other end of it I'll have a foal that can't even compete in the beginner events. fetch the equestrian version of Hercule Poirot, I need to find out who impregnated my horse!

It may not be a plot worthy of Cooper, but it will do for me.

Losing progress in a game is never fun, but imagine spending 11 hours exploring Grand Theft Auto 6 only to discover that none of it was saved. That's exactly what happened to content creator JasonTheWeen, who had a particularly rough launch day after making one unfortunate mistake with his PlayStation 5.

With around 1.3 million followers on YouTube, the content creator had been streaming an extended session of Rockstar's latest adventure. However, after accidentally turning off his console, he returned to the game only to find that his entire 11-hour save was missing!

According to recent reports, according to The Economic Times, he later explained that his foot had accidentally hit the switch on an extension cord, cutting power to his PS5. The moment he realized what had happened was captured live, and his reaction was understandably heartbreaking. Here, take a look:.

In a recent development, visibly devastated, the streamer struggled to hold back tears and repeatedly shouted about the 11 hours he had just lost. He then contacted someone from his team to ask whether there was any way to recover his progress, even if that meant getting back to the beginning of the second chapter rather than having to start the entire adventure again.

Unfortunately, it seems that it wasn’t possible, and he eventually brought a friend to help him rush through the sections he had already completed, hoping to get his marathon back on track.

In a recent development, the exact reason behind the incident remains unclear, but there's a possible explanation involving the game's save system. GTA 6 does feature autosaving, which records progress after completing missions and certain notable events. But that doesn't necessarily mean every action is immediately stored.

One possibility is that JasonTheWeen accidentally turned off his PS5 while the game was writing save data. If that happened, interrupting the process could have corrupted the save file, potentially explaining why so much progress disappeared when he launched the game again.

In a recent development, GTA 6 does feature autosaving, which records progress after completing missions and certain vital events. But that doesn't necessarily mean every action is immediately stored.

We also don't know whether the save can be recovered, so it would be unfair to draw conclusions about the game's autosave system based on this single incident.

Still, the situation is a good reminder that manually saving your progress is worth the extra few seconds. GTA 6 offers multiple manual save slots, allowing players to keep separate backups instead of relying exclusively on autosaving. It has been revealed that unfortunately, losing his progress wasn't the only upsetting moment JasonTheWeen experienced during the stream. Shortly afterward, he heard shouting outside his home and informed viewers that police officers had arrived at his property.

The incident appears to have been a case of swatting, a dangerous prank involving false emergency reports intended to send police officers to someone's home. It's an especially unpleasant situation for any streamer, and it made an already frustrating day considerably worse.

Industry observers note that following the incident, JasonTheWeen also reached out to Rockstar and Sony on social media, asking whether his lost progress could be recovered. For now, there's no confirmed response from either firm about his request or why all the progress was lost.

I’m the host of GTA 6’s “non-stop ‘80s” radio channel Vice City FM. I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I’m the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well! As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!

A rare disease reveals a hidden flaw in the immune system

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1149 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For decades, scientists believed they understood what caused the dangerous inflammation associated with a rare genetic disorder.
  • Industry observers note that the condition, known as mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD), can cause severe inflammatory episodes that are sometimes life-threatening.
  • In a recent development, the researchers found that these cells malfunction in people with MKD, setting off an excessive inflammatory response when infections occur.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For decades, scientists believed they understood what caused the dangerous inflammation associated with a rare genetic disorder. Now, researchers at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research have uncovered evidence that challenges 30 years of established thinking and could open the door to a newly introduced treatment.

Industry observers note that the condition, known as mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD), can cause severe inflammatory episodes that are sometimes life-threatening. A new study published in Immunity identifies a previously underrecognized problem involving natural killer (NK) cells, immune cells that normally help the body eliminate infected cells.

In a recent development, the researchers found that these cells malfunction in people with MKD, setting off an excessive inflammatory response when infections occur. The discovery also points to a possible treatment using existing medications called JAK inhibitors, which could be particularly valuable for patients who do not respond to current therapies.

"This study has revealed a fresh target for this inflammatory disorder and sets the scene for future clinical studies to explore the use of JAK inhibitors or other drugs to neutralize interferon gamma in patients with MKD," indicates Professor Mike Rogers, Lab Head at Garvan and senior author of the study. "This could lead to a targeted treatment that hasn't been tried before.".

Why a Rare Immune Disease Causes Dangerous Inflammation.

MKD is a lifelong condition known to affect hundreds of children and adults around the world, although researchers suspect that many people with the disorder have never been diagnosed. Patients experience recurring attacks of high fever, skin rashes, joint pain, and inflammation in the abdomen. The most serious episodes can cause potentially fatal complications.

Sources indicate that for roughly three decades, research into the disease has largely centered on macrophages, immune cells that help coordinate the body's inflammatory defenses. Existing treatments are designed to block an inflammatory signal released by these cells. However, approximately half of patients do not respond adequately, leaving a major need for better treatment options.

To investigate what might be missing from the prevailing explanation, the Garvan team examined blood samples from people with MKD and studied preclinical models of the disorder.

Sources indicate that their experiments revealed a significant defect in natural killer cells, which play an crucial role in the body's early defenses against viral infections. In MKD, these cells fail to mature properly and struggle to perform one of their most important functions: destroying infected cells before an infection can spread.

Industry observers note that the consequences go beyond an impaired ability to fight infection. When natural killer cells cannot eliminate their targets, they release large amounts of inflammatory signaling molecules, activating other parts of the immune system and potentially triggering widespread inflammation.

According to recent reports, "We found that these immune cells are essentially misfiring," explains Professor Rogers. "NK cells are loaded with toxic ammunition, stored in granules that are released to kill infected cells. However, in MKD these toxic granules can't be released from NK cells and remain trapped inside. When an NK cell fails to kill its target, it compensates by shouting for help, pumping out large amounts of interferon gamma - a powerful inflammatory signal. This activates other immune cells and causes the dangerous fever and widespread inflammation seen in patients.".

Discovery Challenges 30 Years of Immune Disease Research.

The findings suggest that natural killer cell dysfunction, rather than macrophage activity alone, plays a central role in driving MKD.

Dr. Marcia Munoz, Group Leader in the Rogers Lab and lead researcher on the study, claims the results represent a major change in how scientists understand the disease.

Sources indicate that "This really turns on its head 30 years of dogma about what was thought to be the underlying mechanism of disease. In MKD, the primary problem is in NK cells and not in macrophages, as previously believed," she notes.

To investigate how this cellular defect contributes to the disorder, the Garvan researchers collaborated with Professor Mariapia Degli-Esposti and scientists at Monash University.

Using preclinical models, the team established a connection between malfunctioning natural killer cells and the severe symptoms associated with MKD. Their experiments revealed that when the immune system cannot clear a viral infection, the resulting inflammatory response can cause extensive damage to organs.

These results help explain why a disorder involving defective immune defenses can also produce episodes of extreme inflammation.

Existing Drug Highlights Promise for a Upcoming Treatment.

The discovery has already helped guide an experimental treatment approach for a severely affected infant.

Working with doctors at the Royal Children's Hospital in Melbourne, the researchers explored whether baricitinib could reduce the excessive inflammatory signaling associated with MKD.

Baricitinib belongs to a class of medications known as JAK inhibitors. These drugs interfere with signaling pathways used by the immune system, including those involved in responses to interferon gamma. The medication is already used to treat other immune-related conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis and eczema.

Doctors added baricitinib to the infant's existing treatment regimen and subsequently observed an improvement in the child's condition. Inflammatory flare-ups became less frequent, and severe inflammation affecting the gastrointestinal tract began to heal.

Although the results from a single patient cannot establish whether the treatment will work more broadly, the improvement provides encouraging early evidence for a strategy that targets a different part of the inflammatory process.

The researchers believe their findings provide a foundation for future clinical studies investigating JAK inhibitors and other medications that block interferon gamma activity in patients with MKD, particularly those who have not benefited from standard treatments.

Discovery Could Help Explain Other Genetic Diseases.

The potential implications extend beyond MKD itself.

Researchers have introduced the term 'prenylopathies' to describe a family of genetic disorders involving the same metabolic pathway affected in MKD. Early findings suggest that these related diseases may share a similar underlying problem involving natural killer cells that fail to function properly and instead generate excessive inflammatory signals.

If further studies confirm this connection, scientists may be able to identify common disease mechanisms and develop more targeted approaches to diagnosis and treatment across multiple disorders.

"Confirming this link could help end the diagnostic odyssey many patients endure for years or even decades before receiving effective treatment," notes Professor Rogers.

Professor Mike Rogers is a Conjoint Professor at St Vincent's Clinical School, Faculty of Medicine and Health, UNSW Sydney. Dr. Marcia Munoz is a Conjoint Senior Lecturer at St Vincent's Clinical School, Faculty of Medicine and Health, UNSW Sydney.

Materials provided by Garvan Institute of Medical Research. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#5339. Tech Report: Big Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (792 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Big Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Friendslop du jour Big Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!).
  • A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset.
  • It has been revealed that so, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Friendslop du jour Big Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!). House House state that "LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs", and that "well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage", but are quick to note that "generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game.".

A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset. House House explain that they couldn't find a solution themselves, asked a Unity engineer for help who mentioned it was impossible, and then decided the only answer was to ask an LLM chatbot; "after a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code." While absolutely not the most pressing thing to mention here, it is very funny to me for House House to clarify that they "had to modify the suggestion extensively", almost as if this tech isn't actually helpful in giving useful answers.

It has been revealed that so, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove. The thing is, this wasn't a case of being forced to by upper management, as is sometimes the case. This was a choice made entirely voluntarily, and House House are attempting to have their cake and eat it by ending their statement with the reflection that "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards." But then, you know, that's followed up by saying that Big Walk was developed "without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards." So, not to worry, they learned touching the stove is bad by touching the stove, and definitely won't do it again in future. If only there were thousands of other cases informing them why touching the stove is bad.

Very relevant to this reveal is the recent statement by select jurors of the Independent Games Festival which, after much internal deliberation, came to the conclusion that those who sign the statement would decline to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity, with signees including Austin Walker, Sam Barlow, Lena Reine, Brendon Chung, Aura Triolo, aurahack and more. The statement specifies that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms." Fellow juror Liz Ryerson confirmed that Big Walk was being considered by the IGF, and was a matter of discussion in judging as to whether its use of genAI would be acceptable.

As for House House only disclosing this now, they state it was not only because it was necessary for their IGF submission, but also that "we have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage", and that they have spoken on it publicly to Aftermath because "it has become a matter of public interest.".

Industry observers note that if I were to be cynical, I would say that House House would prefer to be the ones breaking this news themselves rather than having the IGF reveal that they had been hiding their use up until now; it's usually easier to control PR if you release it yourself. Major Walk had already been securely in everyone's good books for its support for the BDS boycott, for example, so why ruin that clean rep with something like a genAI disclosure?

I don't know how better to close this article than with an excerpt from that very IGF statement:.

"We know that change does not come at the individual level, but as independent developers, we also know firsthand the value of pushing back on what an industry has deemed "inevitable." As jurists, we feel a responsibility to push past defeatism and aspire to a higher ideal.

It has been revealed that the future is not yet settled. You are not alone. We can stand together.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated on November 19th, 2026 - reformatted and rechecked the list With GTA VI now finally in the hands of players, a decade-plus wait is finally over. But what if you're going to be without your console or PC for a while? How exactly do you get that hit of open-world action when you can't find GTA VI on mobile (yet)?

It has been revealed that well, that's where we come in, with our list of the best mobile games like Grand Theft Auto; covering a huge variety of open-world, crime-focused action games. And, luckily enough, plenty of the classic GTAs are also already on mobile!

Recent findings suggest that yes, while Grove Street Games' mobile ports may be considered a bit lacklustre by some, they're still well-loved for bringing some of the greatest console classics to mobile. And we'll get to them in due course!

Sources indicate that arguably the only 'true' competitor to Grand Theft Auto that saw any measure of success near their level, Saints Row always dove into the wackier, stranger and more glitzy sides of street culture. And with the Third Street Saints ditching their humble origins, when they're brought back to earth, it's up to you to once more become kings of crime in the brand-latest city of Steelport.

Whether it's flopping off of car hoods to defraud insurance, battling zombies with an oversized marital aid or simply speeding through the air on your jet-bike (Volition did it first), Saints Row: The Third offers exciting open-world crime action on mobile that's almost on par with the best GTA has to offer.

A real gem of Rockstar's back catalogue, when it seemed as if they always had something experimental up their sleeve before their attention turned solely to Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption. Bully: Anniversary Edition is a game that was massively controversial as well as beloved by fans.

Set in Bullworth Academy, you play reckless delinquent Jimmy as you navigate the various social cliques, overbearing administration and tedious lessons inflicted on you. And along the way, maybe, just maybe, you'll turn the world of Bullworth upside down in a way no one will forget.

When Rockstar decided they wanted to dust off their quirky, spaghetti-western shooter Red Dead Revolver and give it a brand-latest GTA-style makeover, I think few expected it to be as popular as it became.

Playing as John Marston, you'll ride the range of the American West in pursuit of your former comrades-in-crime, with the intent of saving your family and maybe your own soul along the way. Expect shootouts, bank robberies, cattle rustling and maybe a few zombies along the way.

One of many GTA Online-likes to try and recreate the open-world crime experience on mobile, just with fewer Shark Cards, Grand Outlaws is another recent release well worth looking into. While its more colourful setting may clash with what you expect from a gritty crime thriller, and it looks more Fortnite than Sleeping Dogs, it's still got plenty of appeal for those wanting something GTA-style in their lives.

Probably one of the largest-scale competitors in the GTA Online-likes scene, OneState is one to go for if you prefer a more realistic interpretation of open-world crime and action than Grand Outlaws. Its realistic recreation of Los Angeles even boasts a near-future, plausible version of real-life developments.

Industry observers note that about the only thing to be aware of when it comes to OneState is that this is an RP game first and foremost, and you'll be just as likely to fall into the role of firefighter or EMT as a crime kingpin. But if that depth of realism is what you're hunting for, OneState is sure to satisfy.

A really unique (as much as my editors hate using that word) entry in the Grand Theft Auto series, Chinatown Wars takes you back to Liberty City. But rather than exploring the mafia connections, you'll be joining the deadly world of the triads.

Set from a top-down perspective like the classic entries in the series, Chinatown Wars boasts interesting minigames, the same level of violence and chaos as you'd expect, as well as a sprawling narrative of revenge and ambition.

Download now! Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars Max Payne.

Recent findings suggest that are we breaking from the trend of 'open world' here? Sure, absolutely. But Max Payne, first released by Remedy and later acquired by Rockstar, is undoubtedly full of the same gunplay and thrilling crime storylines as any GTA entry. And, I'd argue, that its actual gunplay is leagues ahead of what Grand Theft Auto has ever offered.

According to recent reports, set in Newly introduced York during the middle of a snowstorm, you play as the gritty police detective Max Payne as you shoot your way through hordes of mafia goons. The bullet-time mechanic still holds up years later, and if you need a short, sharp hit of shootout action, then Max Payne is one to grab.

Download now! Max Payne Mobile Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories.

Recent findings suggest that another one-off entry in the brief portable series that Rockstar had, which includes Vice City Stories (sadly not available on mobile). In Liberty City Stories, you return once more to the 3D incarnation of their Upcoming York analogue, before it got a major makeover for Grand Theft Auto IV.

Playing as Toni Cipriani, you'll be working closely with the mafia and experience Liberty City and what it was like before Grand Theft Auto III. Definitely one to play if you were a fan of watching The Sopranos, and if you're just a substantial fan of delving into the history of GTA as a universe!

And now for something completely different... Okay, not that different. But Neverness to Everness is undoubtedly one to play only if you're willing to really stretch the definition of a GTA-like. Rather than a realistic city or characters, you'll be jumping into anime-inspired action with flashy combat and a sprawling metropolis.

Recent findings suggest that but even if you are fighting on the right side of the law, Neverness to Everness tries to lean into the mayhem of GTA just as much as any other. And while it's had some controversial issues with AI, at its core it's still got plenty of the same fun to be had on the go as Grand Theft Auto.

A Gameloft production for mobile, Gangstar Vegas may be the lesser pick on this list. But, purely for curiosity's sake it's well worth looking at for its ambition alone. Released back in 2013, Gangstar Vegas was arguably the first mobile game to try and match what GTA had to offer, full 3D world included.

In a recent development, boasting all the same glitz, glamour and grime as GTA, not to mention the always-fun Las Vegas setting, Gangstar Vegas: World of Crime is rightly regarded as a flawed, but lovable cult classic that really highlights how difficult it is to pin down the formula. Still, it gets more than a few points for trying.

Download now! Gangstar Vegas Honourable Mention: Other GTA Ports If what you want is just GTA, name included, then mobile is pretty chock-a-block with them. We've got Vice City, San Andreas, Chinatown Wars and Grand Theft Auto III all available to play on your choice of iOS or Android. Not to mention the er, Definitive Edition ports too.

According to recent reports, but, as you may well know, these are ports where a lot of rough edges can be seen. While not quite as shoddy as the infamous Definitive Collection, Grove Street Games' ports of the original 3D trilogy are definitely not the best way to experience them, but on mobile they're all feature-complete and almost as good as you remember them; keyword being 'almost'. And with that in mind, those are some of the best, if not the best, ways to experience GTA-like action on mobile while you're away from your console or PC! And if you want to relive the classics, you've also got options with the available ports. So, when you need to take a break from GTA VI, you're still spoilt for choice on mobile.

It has been revealed that gen.G still leave with US$800,000 as runners-up. Semi-finalists T1 and Invictus Gaming received US$400,000 each. Riot ran the event from 15 October to 14 November with 19 teams.

Gen.G’s admission points to the draft as a weak spot. The figures support a narrower reading too. Gen.G swept both knockout opponents before the final. Against BLG, they could not hold the lead after taking the opening game.

It has been revealed that worlds was BLG’s second international trophy of the year. In March they won the First Stand Tournament in São Paulo. They beat G2 Esports 3-1 in that final and collected the US$250,000 top prize.

Winning both events makes BLG the first team since SK Telecom T1 in 2016 to take more than one major international title in a year.

To everyone who’s ever worn the jersey, worked behind the scenes, or cheered us on: we did it!#BLGWIN #Worlds2026 pic.twitter.com/E2TIgNfhgv.

— Bilibili Gaming (@BilibiliGaming) November 15, 2026.

The 2027 Mid-Season Invitational will be held in Valencia.
